tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30.

| # | Skill | Runs (60 d) | Why it is on the list | Care |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `forecast-capture` | 12 | Weekly in-season Big 12 forecast freeze. | Mid-season: audit on a non-Wednesday, and change nothing that alters a capture already made. |
| 2 | `project` | 6 | The portfolio registry and board; weekly-review's sweep reads the same registry. | `portfolio.json` has write-provenance rules (Tier A `portfolio-registry-write-provenance`). |
| 3 | `codex-review` | 4 | Codex reviews a plan in a bounded loop; the audit Method calls `codex exec` directly, not this skill. | Overlaps `claudex-loop` mode=review: check which one Eric actually runs before fixing both. |
| 4 | `ingest-book` | 2 | Turns a whole book into vault notes; the costliest atomization run. | Tier A `ingest-review-gate`: Eric reviews before any costly run. Test on a short source, never a full book unasked. |
| 5 | `name-meetings` | 2 | Renames Fireflies meetings with generic titles; meeting-sync calls it. | Renames go to the Fireflies API (outside service): test the detect step only; applying renames waits for Eric. |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.
4. **Fix**: real bugs first, then the writing-for-agents pass (steps in run order, a **Done when** line, positive rules, one home per fact, reference only some runs need moved to a sibling file). A script fix that adds a branch gets a small test.
5. **Test** by running the skill for real where it is safe. Data sent to an outside service (Jev, email, Teams) waits for Eric.
6. **Codex review**: `codex exec -s read-only "<prompt>" < /dev/null` on the diff (without `< /dev/null` it can wait on stdin forever), output to `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-<topic>-<date>.{md,txt}`. Check each finding before fixing it.
7. **Close**: portability check (`python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`), commit by path in each repo touched, push, and add a line to `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md` (and the touched repo's own STATUS).

| 2026-10-30 | `weekly-review` | skills `db60b87`, `8e0ea63`, `fe6b76b` | No `python` on the Mac; `--agent` emptied Fireflies rows; one ask with picks. |
| 2026-10-30 | `backup` | skills `ab87c9d`, `3d15e0d`, `fe6b76b`; dotclaude `d6ab8bc`, `8fcfb93` | Stale 21:00 schedule; a dry run could hide a failed day. |

ignores `argument-hint` / `allowed-tools`. Codex over-fires without the negative clause;

   it is also how the cut reaches Windows.** Undo with

   (`skills-archive/` is not in the repo and never reaches the other machine).

   98 of the 99 archived skills were still live in the pool (306 entries there vs 61
   canonical). Claude Code stopped seeing them; **Pi auto-discovers that folder**, so
   installing Pi would have re-exposed all of them. Always cut both.
3. **Skills live in three places and it is easy to edit the wrong copy.**
   `~/.claude/skills/` (19 entries were symlinks pointing *out* to the pool),
   `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork), `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex, 27 symlinks + 5 real
   dirs). Count with `find -L`; plain `find` undercounts.
4. **`sync-to-codex.sh` did `rm -rf "$dst/$s"; cp -R "$SRC/$s"`** over a 7-name
   allowlist. If `$SRC/$s` ever became a symlink into `$dst`, that deletes the real
   data. `dev-sync` tells you to run it after every pull. A `.ps1` twin has the same
   shape — patch both.
5. **`~/.claude/skills/_shared/`** holds `config.json` + `Inference/` and is resolved by
   10+ skills via `parents[2]/_shared/config.json`. It has **no SKILL.md**. Never treat
   "no SKILL.md" as "orphan, delete".
6. **"606 plugin skills" is cache, not load.** Only 6 of 24 plugins are enabled
   (~37 skills exposed). The rest are disabled plugins and old cached versions.

## Executed 2026-09-12 — traps the live run found

- **Views are live links now.** `~/.agents/skills/<owned>` and `~/.codex/skills/<owned>`
  point into canonical, so anything that writes a view path writes canonical
  (`graphify install --platform agents` does; see [[graphify-runtime-setup]]).

  ignore that file, so an owned skill set `"off"` there is hidden in Claude Code but live
  elsewhere. Perfect frontmatter does not help; `skill-portability-check.py` fails it.
  Resolved 2026-09-13: Eric re-enabled the 7 (ArXiv, ISA, Science, capture-insight,
  library-review, pp-espn, session-miner) — `~/.claude` commit `21c686d`, checker 42/42.
  Never set an owned skill "off" again; retire it from canonical instead.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

Two branches: **Write** (add, replace, remove a fact) and **Recall** (answer from past context). Take the one the request needs.

## Tiers

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across projects?" Yes → Tier A. Work in play now → Tier B.

**Tier A: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`**, one file per fact, indexed by that folder's `MEMORY.md`.

| Fact | File | `metadata.type` |
|---|---|---|
| Durable user fact | `user_<name>.md` | `user` |
| Stable project convention or gotcha | `project_<name>.md` | `project` |
| Behavior rule from Eric | `feedback_<name>.md` | `feedback` |
| Pointer to an outside system | `reference_<name>.md` | `reference` |

- **Slug**: use the memory folder the harness names in this session's system prompt. It is the absolute cwd with every non-letter, non-digit folded to `-` (`~/DEV/CLI_Dev` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV-CLI-Dev`).
- **Machine**: write to this machine's slug (Mac: `-Users-kristinarash-*`). The other machine never auto-injects it. Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/`, which both machines and the cloud see.
- **`name:`** is the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased: `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` → `project-idea-capture`. `[[links]]` target this bare name. (A 2026-09-02 audit found the corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. `remember.py` enforces the rule.)

**Tier B: `~/.claude/global-memory/`**, two capped files. Caps are in characters, and only this skill enforces them: the SessionStart hook (`~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`) injects both files whole.

| Fact | Home | Cap |
|---|---|---|
| In-progress work | `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads` (max 5; park one to add one) | 2,500 |
| Paused work | `MEMORY.md` `## Parked` | (same file) |
| Current env notes | `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes` | (same file) |
| Decisions waiting on Eric | `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions` | (same file) |
| Durable user profile | `USER.md` | 1,375 |

USER.md holds only the profile lines every session needs. Detail about Eric goes to a Tier A `user_` file.

## Write

1. **Pick the tier** with the tables above.
2. **Dedup.** Tier A: grep the slug's folder for the fact's key words (`grep -ril '<word>' <memory folder>`) and read every hit. `remember.py` checks only names, not content. Tier B: read the target file in full. If the fact exists, replace it in place; that is the default over adding.
3. **Write it.**
   - **Tier A add or replace**, one call, run from the project folder (`--dir <memory folder>` overrides):
     `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/remember.py --type <t> --name <bare-name> --desc "<one line>" --hook "<when to open>" [--why "..." --how "..."] "<fact>"`
     It writes the file and the index line, reads both back, and refreshes recall.py's index. Exit 0 prints `PASS`. Exit 2 means the name exists or looks alike: read that file, then rerun with `--type <its type> --name <its name> --update`, or add `--force` for a genuinely new fact. Exit 1 is a `FAIL`; fix the input it names.
   - **Tier A replace of a legacy file** (underscores after the type, like `project_kenny_boyd.md`; ~40 exist): `remember.py` would write a second file. Edit the old file in place and keep its index line.
   - **Tier B**: measure first, `python3 -c "import sys;print(len(open(sys.argv[1]).read()))" ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or `USER.md`). If the write would pass the cap, merge or prune stale lines first. Then edit under the right `##` section.
   - **Remove (either tier)**: ask Eric first. Tier A: delete the file and its line in the slug's `MEMORY.md`; recall.py drops the file on its next run. Tier B: delete the line.
4. **Verify.**
   - Tier A: `remember.py`'s `PASS` covers read-back, the `name`/`description`/`type` frontmatter lines, and one index pointer. After a hand edit, check those three yourself.
   - Tier B: read the file back. The fact appears once, in the intended section, and the character count is at or under the cap.
   - Both: read the surrounding section for a contradiction or stale twin, and resolve it.
5. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

**Done when** the fact is in one home, every check in step 4 passed, and the confirmation is sent. On a failed check, report `FAIL`, the path, and the check instead of the confirmation.

USER.md and MEMORY.md are a frozen snapshot, injected once at session start to keep the prompt cache. A write persists now and is active next session; the one-line confirmation is the whole announcement.

## Recall

Climb in order. Stop as soon as the question is answered.

1. **Tier 0**: what is already in context: USER.md, MEMORY.md, and this folder's Tier A index. Zero cost.
2. **L1**: `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "question"`. Plain code, ~1 s: keyword rank over the memsearch roots, the whole vault, and every `projects/*/memory` folder. It opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs; on a weak match it also runs memsearch (~10 s). If the paragraphs miss, open the #2 or #3 candidate it lists.
3. **L2**: `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "<reworded question>" --deep`. Always adds memsearch's hybrid meaning search (~10 s), memory files first.
4. **L3**: `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`: the full section around a hit.
5. **L4**: `memsearch transcript <session_id>`: raw dialogue. Last resort.
6. **Fallback**: "I don't have a record of that."

The daily compiled logs (`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`) arrive as a pointer, not content. Open one when the question names that day. Only `claude-memory-compiler` writes them.

**A wrong or stale recall becomes a bench question, unasked.** When Eric corrects a recalled fact, or a newer file proves your recalled answer stale, in the same session:

1. Add one row to `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/questions.tsv`: `miss`, the question as asked, the file holding the right answer, the right answer in one line (tab-separated).
2. Run `CSET=miss bash ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/run.sh C` (~Remember:.06 a question) and note the result in that folder's `results.md`.
3. Run `python3 -I ~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/check.py`. When it prints `OK`, run it again with `--update-baseline`. The daily backup's check guards each question that was a hit in `baseline.json`, so the new question is guarded only after this update, and only once recall.py ranks it first. On a `DROP`, report it and leave the baseline alone.
4. Tell Eric in one line.

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30.

| # | Skill | Runs (60 d) | Why it is on the list | Care |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `forecast-capture` | 12 | Weekly in-season Big 12 forecast freeze. | Mid-season: audit on a non-Wednesday, and change nothing that alters a capture already made. |
| 2 | `project` | 6 | The portfolio registry and board; weekly-review's sweep reads the same registry. | `portfolio.json` has write-provenance rules (Tier A `portfolio-registry-write-provenance`). |
| 3 | `codex-review` | 4 | Codex reviews a plan in a bounded loop; the audit Method calls `codex exec` directly, not this skill. | Overlaps `claudex-loop` mode=review: check which one Eric actually runs before fixing both. |
| 4 | `ingest-book` | 2 | Turns a whole book into vault notes; the costliest atomization run. | Tier A `ingest-review-gate`: Eric reviews before any costly run. Test on a short source, never a full book unasked. |
| 5 | `name-meetings` | 2 | Renames Fireflies meetings with generic titles; meeting-sync calls it. | Renames go to the Fireflies API (outside service): test the detect step only; applying renames waits for Eric. |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.
4. **Fix**: real bugs first, then the writing-for-agents pass (steps in run order, a **Done when** line, positive rules, one home per fact, reference only some runs need moved to a sibling file). A script fix that adds a branch gets a small test.
5. **Test** by running the skill for real where it is safe. Data sent to an outside service (Jev, email, Teams) waits for Eric.
6. **Codex review**: `codex exec -s read-only "<prompt>" < /dev/null` on the diff (without `< /dev/null` it can wait on stdin forever), output to `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-<topic>-<date>.{md,txt}`. Check each finding before fixing it.
7. **Close**: portability check (`python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`), commit by path in each repo touched, push, and add a line to `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md` (and the touched repo's own STATUS).

## Done

| Date | Skill | Commits | Headline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-25 | `closeout` | skills `740138a` (review: `~/.claude/audits/2026-10-25-closeout-skill-review.md`) | Steps in run order; done line. |
| 2026-10-25 | `claude-stack-doctor` | skills `31e7631` | Split into SKILL + FIXES + WINDOWS; false OKs fixed. |
| 2026-10-30 | `doctor-plus` | skills `ef2e377`, `be02868` | User-invoked; steps and done line; one report home. |
| 2026-10-30 | `weekly-review` | skills `db60b87`, `8e0ea63`, `fe6b76b` | No `python` on the Mac; `--agent` emptied Fireflies rows; one ask with picks. |
| 2026-10-30 | `backup` | skills `ab87c9d`, `3d15e0d`, `fe6b76b`; dotclaude `d6ab8bc`, `8fcfb93` | Stale 21:00 schedule; a dry run could hide a failed day. |
| 2026-10-30 | `meeting-sync`, `fireflies-intake` | skills `dfd95d1`, `37f93fc`, `fe6b76b`; KeystoneOS `13f7dbf`, `bf1250d` | 06:00 job exported first, so rename and Jev tag never ran. |
| 2026-10-30 | `memory-write` | skills `7a9dd89`; dotclaude `d6fa209` | Tier 0 claimed the daily log (pointer only); bench check counted hits, so a new question was never guarded. |
| 2026-10-30 | `dev-sync` | skills `be6bce0`; dotclaude `a29d6b0` | Nothing synced `claude-memory-compiler`, or `SecondBrain` on a day the backup skipped; missing nested repos cloned to the top level. |
| 2026-10-30 | `startup` | skills `908a5a4`; dotclaude `a37a767`; SportScienceResearchRepo `e34ced7` | First real run since the 10-29 rebuild: works; answered/repeated decisions kept showing (script hides only items that start with ANSWERED/RESOLVED). |

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state
- 2026-10-30 (Fri): Week 9 captured, 16/16 teams. Week 8 graded 2 of 8 sides. Baylor 5.94 expected wins (raw 5-7); UCF that night 37%. Nothing lost from the missed Wed 10-28.

## Gotchas
- `uv run --with playwright` pulls the newest playwright. When it updates, the capture dies with `Executable doesn't exist at .../chromium-<N>`. Fix: `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium`, then re-run.

- One failed attempt per team is normal; the retry recovers it.

- CFBD dates a TBD kickoff at 00:00 UTC, the evening before in Central. `market_view.py` uses a 6-day window so next week's TBD games stay out.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/name-meetings

# Name Meetings

Eric does not name most Fireflies recordings, and an unnamed one exports to the vault as `2026-10-29_Oct_29_0944_AM.md`. This skill finds generic titles, proposes real ones from the AI summary, and writes the approved ones back to Fireflies, the source of truth. `scripts/rename.py` is the only write path: it verifies every write by reading the title back (the CLI and the MCP rename tools are broken; [REFERENCE.md → Why renames bypass the CLI and MCP](REFERENCE.md#why-renames-bypass-the-cli-and-mcp)).

Detail lives in [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md); load only the section a step names. Below, `R=~/.claude/skills/name-meetings/scripts/rename.py`.

## Steps

1. **Auth.** `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` must show `"auth": "configured"`. Otherwise stop and give Eric the fix from `pp-fireflies` → Auth Setup.

2. **Resume the ledger.** The pending-renames file is `pending_renames_file` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` ([REFERENCE.md → Pending-renames file](REFERENCE.md#pending-renames-file)). If `pending[]` has entries, they are already approved: say "Resuming N pending renames" and run `python3 $R --pending` (step 6 explains its output). A `STOP` here ends the writing for this run: go to step 7 if any line was `OK`, otherwise to step 8. Entries in `review[]` join the step 5 table as candidates; in Unattended mode they stay where they are.

3. **List the window.** Refresh the local DB in full, then list id, local date, title and speakers:

   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent
   fireflies-pp-cli transcripts find --from 30 --processed-only --limit 100000 --json --no-input \
     | python3 -c 'import json,sys,datetime as D
   for x in json.load(sys.stdin):
       t = D.datetime.fromisoformat(x["dateString"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone()
       print(x["id"], t.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), json.dumps(x["title"]), "speakers=" + ",".join(s["name"] for s in x.get("speakers") or []))'
   ```

   Change `--from` when Eric names a window ("last 60 days"); without it `find` covers all time, which is slow to rename. When meeting-sync passes ids, keep only those. The flags each fix a trap ([REFERENCE.md → CLI gotchas](REFERENCE.md#cli-gotchas)): `--full` so the list is current, `--limit 100000` past the default 100, and no `--agent`, whose compact output drops the date and speakers.

4. **Detect generics.** Match each title against [REFERENCE.md → Generic-title patterns](REFERENCE.md#generic-title-patterns). Every other title is curated and stays as it is, including Eric's `Series_MMDDYYYY` names (`StaffMeet_10222026`).

   The list can hold **ghosts**: meetings deleted from Fireflies that `sync --full` never prunes. Nothing in a read tells them apart, so keep every candidate regardless of age; the write in step 6 reports a ghost as `GONE` ([REFERENCE.md → Deleted transcripts](REFERENCE.md#deleted-transcripts-linger-in-the-local-db)).

5. **Propose, then approve.** For each candidate read the summary first:

   ```bash
   fireflies-pp-cli summary <id> --format gist --json --agent
   ```

   Build the title from the gist, keywords, overview and the step 3 speakers, by [REFERENCE.md → Title construction rules](REFERENCE.md#title-construction-rules). A meeting in one of Eric's recurring series takes the series name; a gist too vague to name gets `[skip — gist too vague]`, for Eric to name in the Fireflies UI. When several candidates come from one event, ask Eric what the event was and offer a shared prefix.

   Show a table `# | Date | Current | Proposed | Action` (`✓` apply, `—` skip), then `AskUserQuestion` "How should I apply these renames?" with **Approve all / Edit rows / Apply subset / Cancel**. Edit rows: ask which rows and what titles, then confirm the revised table. Apply subset: ask which rows ("1,3,5", "skip 2,4"). Cancel: end the run with nothing applied.

6. **Apply.** Add each approved row to `pending[]` as `{"id": "<meetingId>", "title": "<title>"}`, keeping what the file already holds and removing any `review[]` entry for that id, then run `python3 $R --pending`. It spaces the writes, verifies each by read-back and rewrites the file. Read its lines, never just the exit code:
   - `OK` verified; gone from `pending[]`.
   - `FAIL` transient (timeout, 5xx, read-back mismatch); stays in `pending[]` for the next run.
   - `GONE` permanent (`Transcript not found`, a title under 5 or over 256 characters, a malformed entry); dropped. Report it as unrenamable, with the reason.
   - `STOP` rate limited; the rest stay in `pending[]`. Make no more writes this run; step 7 still verifies the `OK` ones.

   When both arrays are empty afterwards, delete the file.

7. **Wait, re-sync, verify.** Fireflies' list endpoint (what `sync` and `find` read) lags the single-transcript endpoint `rename.py` verifies against by minutes. Run `sleep 270` as a background Bash job, then `fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent` and the step 3 list again, and confirm each new title. A title still old after the wait means more lag: wait and re-sync once more. The rename already verified, so the fix is waiting; a second rename can clobber a good title.
   - A plain `sync` (no `--full`) never picks up title edits yet exits 0 with `total: 0`; the re-run list is the proof.
   - If the sync fails twice, the renames still stand in Fireflies; only the local DB is stale. Say so and give the command: `fireflies-pp-cli sync --full --resources transcripts --agent`.
   - Generics you never proposed mean the step 3 DB was stale: name them and offer a second pass.
   - A renamed meeting already in the vault (its id is in meeting-sync's `.sync-state.json`) keeps its generic filename; re-export makes a second file. Name it in the report and point to meeting-sync's filename drift audit (`DRIFT.md`).

8. **Report**, 3–5 lines: N scanned / M generic · K applied · F left in `pending[]` (next run resumes) · G gone · S skipped for manual naming · re-sync status (verified, or the stale-DB warning) · vault files left with a generic name.

**Done when** every generic title in the window is verified renamed in the step 7 list, queued in `pending[]` or `review[]`, or named in the report as skipped or gone, and the report says whether the local DB matches Fireflies.

## Unattended mode

Only when the calling skill declares it (meeting-sync does, in its step 2, scoped to the ids it passes). Every step runs as above, summaries and proposals included; only step 5's approval table and question are replaced, by the confidence gate in [REFERENCE.md → Unattended mode](REFERENCE.md#unattended-mode): rows that pass go to `pending[]` and are applied; every other row is appended to `review[]` for Eric's next interactive run. With no generic titles among the ids, return to the caller with nothing to report. This is the only path that renames without Eric's approval.

class TestUndoSafety(ServerCase):
    """The undo snapshot can be hours old. Restoring it blind would silently erase
    anything the CLI or the `project` skill wrote in the meantime — including
    `ideas`, which this page does not render at all, so the loss would be invisible.
    """

    def registry(self):
        return json.loads(self.get("/api/registry").read())

    def external_write(self):
        """Stand-in for `portfolio.py add-idea` running in a terminal."""
        path = self.dir / "portfolio.json"
        data = portfolio.load_registry(path)
        portfolio.add_idea(data, "an idea captured outside the board")
        portfolio.save_registry(path, data)

    def refused_undo(self):
        self.post("/api/project/A", {"status": "paused"})
        self.external_write()
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as cm:
            self.post("/api/undo", {})
        return cm.exception

    def test_undo_after_an_external_write_returns_409(self):
        exc = self.refused_undo()
        self.assertEqual(exc.code, 409)
        self.assertIn("outside the board", json.loads(exc.read())["error"])
        exc.close()

    def test_the_external_write_survives_a_refused_undo(self):
        self.refused_undo().close()
        data = self.registry()
        self.assertEqual(len(data["ideas"]), 1)                     # not destroyed
        self.assertEqual(data["projects"][0]["status"], "paused")   # board write kept

    def test_a_refused_undo_clears_the_buffer(self):
        self.refused_undo().close()
        with self.assertRaises(urllib.error.HTTPError) as cm:
            self.post("/api/undo", {})

def idea_name(data: dict, pitch: str, name: str | None = None) -> str:
    """A unique `[A-Za-z0-9_]` name for a new inbox card.

    Unique across inbox[] and projects[]: board_ops finds inbox records by name,
    so a twin would make promote/archive/delete act on the wrong card. The name
    also becomes the dev_folder on promotion, hence the narrow character set.
    """
    base = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", name or "").strip("_")
    if not base:
        words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", pitch)[:4]
        base = "_".join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:] for w in words) or "Idea"
    taken = {r.get("name") for r in data.get("inbox", [])} | {p.get("name") for p in data.get("projects", [])}
    candidate, n = base, 2
    while candidate in taken:
        candidate, n = f"{base}_{n}", n + 1
    return candidate


def add_idea(data: dict, pitch: str, source: str = "", name: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Capture an idea as an inbox card, the list the board shows (2026-10-31).

    It used to append to `ideas[]`, which the board never renders, so captured
    ideas were invisible there. `ideas[]` stays as history.
    """
    if not pitch.strip():
        raise RegistryError("idea pitch is empty")
    card_name = idea_name(data, pitch, name)
    record = {
        "name": card_name,
        "dev_folder": card_name,
        "source": source,
        "status": "paused",
        "purpose": pitch.strip(),
        "captured_at": _dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }
    data.setdefault("inbox", []).append(record)
    return record

    Unique across inbox[] and projects[]: board_ops finds inbox records by name,
    so a twin would make promote/archive/delete act on the wrong card. The name
    also becomes the dev_folder on promotion, hence the narrow character set.
    """
    base = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", name or "").strip("_")
    if not base:
        words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", pitch)[:4]
        base = "_".join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:] for w in words) or "Idea"
    taken = {r.get("name") for r in data.get("inbox", [])} | {p.get("name") for p in data.get("projects", [])}
    candidate, n = base, 2
    while candidate in taken:
        candidate, n = f"{base}_{n}", n + 1
    return candidate


def add_idea(data: dict, pitch: str, source: str = "", name: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Capture an idea as an inbox card, the list the board shows (2026-10-31).

    It used to append to `ideas[]`, which the board never renders, so captured
    ideas were invisible there. `ideas[]` stays as history.
    """
    if not pitch.strip():
        raise RegistryError("idea pitch is empty")
    card_name = idea_name(data, pitch, name)
    record = {
        "name": card_name,
        "dev_folder": card_name,
        "source": source,
        "status": "paused",
        "purpose": pitch.strip(),
        "captured_at": _dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }
    data.setdefault("inbox", []).append(record)
    return record

        data = {"meta": {}, "ideas": [], "inbox": [{"name": "Course_Builder_Agent_On"}],

        self.assertEqual(rec["status"], "paused")
        self.assertEqual(data["ideas"], [])
        self.assertIs(data["inbox"][-1], rec)

        data = {"meta": {}, "ideas": [], "projects": []}
        rec = portfolio.add_idea(data, "x", name="ARC / research council")

    def test_empty_pitch_is_refused(self):
        with self.assertRaises(portfolio.RegistryError):
            portfolio.add_idea({"meta": {}, "ideas": [], "projects": []}, "   ")

from pathlib import Path

PT = Path.home() / "DEV/project-triage"
sys.path.insert(0, str(PT))
import portfolio  # noqa: E402

NAMES = {  # pitch prefix -> card name
    "Content-creation agent": "Content_Creation_Agent",
    "Intern curriculum development agent": "Intern_Curriculum_Agent",
    "Course-builder agent": "Course_Builder_Agent",
}

waiting = [i for i in data["ideas"] if i.get("status") == "inbox"]
assert len(waiting) == 3, f"expected 3 waiting ideas, found {len(waiting)}"
for idea in waiting:
    name = next(n for prefix, n in NAMES.items() if idea["pitch"].startswith(prefix))

    idea["status"] = "promoted"                       # history stays in ideas[]
    print("moved:", rec["name"])
portfolio.validate(data)
portfolio.save_registry(path, data)
print("inbox now:", [r["name"] for r in data["inbox"]])

`promote` and `rank` change `portfolio.json` through `portfolio.load_registry` /
`save_registry`, run from `$PT` (see SKILL.md, Paths). Use these functions, not the Edit
tool: `save_registry` validates the whole file first, refreshes `portfolio.json.bak` the
way the CLI and the board do (the provenance check in Tier A memory reads it), and
replaces the file atomically while the board polls it. Load, change and save in one
script, as below, so a board edit has well under a second to land in between.

A refused save raises `RegistryError: <problems>` and leaves the file unchanged: show it
verbatim and stop.

## promote `<idea>`

1. Find the idea: `ideas[]` rows with `status: inbox` whose `pitch` matches. One match, or
   ask Eric which.
2. Check `projects[]` for a row that already carries this idea (another session may have
   added it). If one exists, only set the idea's `status` to `promoted` and say so.
3. Ask Eric for the lane (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`), the project name

   action. Take `purpose` as one line from the pitch.
4. Save the row as paused, then start it with the CLI, which stamps `started` and gives
   the row its rank in the lane. The `&&` runs the start only after a clean save; if the
   start then fails, the row stays paused: show the error and stop.

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF' && python3 portfolio.py set-status "<Project_Name>" active --note "promoted from the ideas list"
import datetime as dt
from pathlib import Path
import portfolio as pf
p = Path("portfolio.json"); d = pf.load_registry(p)
idea = [i for i in d["ideas"] if i["status"] == "inbox" and "<words from the pitch>" in i["pitch"]]
assert len(idea) == 1, [i["pitch"][:60] for i in idea]
name = "<Project_Name>"
assert not any(x["name"].lower() == name.lower() for x in d["projects"]), f"{name} exists"
idea[0]["status"] = "promoted"
d["projects"].append({
    "name": name, "dev_folder": "<DEV folder, or the name>", "lane": "<lane>",
    "rank": 10**6, "status": "paused", "stage": "idea",
    "purpose": "<one line>", "next_action": "<next action>",
    "links": [], "updates": [], "source": f"idea {idea[0].get('captured_at', '')[:10]}",
    "curated_at": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
})
pf.save_registry(p, d)
print("saved", name)
EOF
```

## rank

The board shows each lane as stage columns (an `unstaged` column, then `idea` → `shipped`),
and `rank` orders the cards within a column. Board drags and card edits renumber the lane
stage by stage. So a rank order holds only within a stage.

1. Show the lane's active rows grouped by stage, in current `rank` order, and ask Eric for
   his order. If his order crosses stages, tell him the stage grouping wins.
2. Apply exactly his order: his rows take temporary ranks below 1 in that order, then the
   board's own renumbering (`_renumber`, which also numbers the lane's paused rows) gives
   every row its final rank:

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import portfolio as pf, board_ops
p = Path("portfolio.json"); d = pf.load_registry(p)
lane, order = "<lane>", ["<Name1>", "<Name2>"]   # Eric's order: active or paused rows only
for i, name in enumerate(order):
    row = board_ops.find(d, name)
    assert row["lane"] == lane and row["status"] in ("active", "paused"), name
    row["rank"] = i - len(order)                  # temporary; renumbered next line
board_ops._renumber(d, lane)
pf.save_registry(p, d)
print([(x["name"], x["rank"], x.get("stage")) for x in board_ops.live(d, lane) if x["status"] == "active"])
EOF
```

3. Show Eric the printed order.

# Registry edits with no CLI command

`promote` and `rank` change `portfolio.json` through `portfolio.load_registry` /
`save_registry`, run from `$PT` (see SKILL.md, Paths). Use these functions, not the Edit
tool: `save_registry` validates the whole file first, refreshes `portfolio.json.bak` the
way the CLI and the board do (the provenance check in Tier A memory reads it), and
replaces the file atomically while the board polls it. Load, change and save in one
script, as below, so a board edit has well under a second to land in between.

A refused save raises `RegistryError: <problems>` and leaves the file unchanged: show it
verbatim and stop.

## promote `<idea>`

1. Find the idea: `ideas[]` rows with `status: inbox` whose `pitch` matches. One match, or
   ask Eric which.
2. Check `projects[]` for a row that already carries this idea (another session may have
   added it). If one exists, only set the idea's `status` to `promoted` and say so.
3. Ask Eric for the lane (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`), the project name
   (`Words_With_Underscores`, matching the DEV folder when there is one), and the next
   action. Take `purpose` as one line from the pitch.
4. Save the row as paused, then start it with the CLI, which stamps `started` and gives
   the row its rank in the lane. The `&&` runs the start only after a clean save; if the
   start then fails, the row stays paused: show the error and stop.


## rank

The board shows each lane as stage columns (an `unstaged` column, then `idea` → `shipped`),
and `rank` orders the cards within a column. Board drags and card edits renumber the lane
stage by stage. So a rank order holds only within a stage.

1. Show the lane's active rows grouped by stage, in current `rank` order, and ask Eric for
   his order. If his order crosses stages, tell him the stage grouping wins.
2. Apply exactly his order: his rows take temporary ranks below 1 in that order, then the
   board's own renumbering (`_renumber`, which also numbers the lane's paused rows) gives
   every row its final rank:

```
cd "$PT" && python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import portfolio as pf, board_ops
p = Path("portfolio.json"); d = pf.load_registry(p)
lane, order = "<lane>", ["<Name1>", "<Name2>"]   # Eric's order: active or paused rows only
for i, name in enumerate(order):
    row = board_ops.find(d, name)
    assert row["lane"] == lane and row["status"] in ("active", "paused"), name
    row["rank"] = i - len(order)                  # temporary; renumbered next line
board_ops._renumber(d, lane)
pf.save_registry(p, d)
print([(x["name"], x["rank"], x.get("stage")) for x in board_ops.live(d, lane) if x["status"] == "active"])
EOF
```

3. Show Eric the printed order.

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).
- **Audit agents run on Sonnet (Eric, 2026-10-31).** When audits run as subagents, pass `model: "sonnet"`. Never Haiku. Parallel agents each edit only their own skill, commit by path, and never push; the main session updates this file and pushes once at the end.

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30; this five picked 2026-10-31.

Eric's local runner patch forces `gpt-6-astra` at low effort and breaks one unit test (10-31 codex-review audit). |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.
4. **Fix**: real bugs first, then the writing-for-agents pass (steps in run order, a **Done when** line, positive rules, one home per fact, reference only some runs need moved to a sibling file). A script fix that adds a branch gets a small test.
5. **Test** by running the skill for real where it is safe. Data sent to an outside service (Jev, email, Teams) waits for Eric.
6. **Codex review**: `codex exec -s read-only "<prompt>" < /dev/null` on the diff (without `< /dev/null` it can wait on stdin forever), output to `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-<topic>-<date>.{md,txt}`. Check each finding before fixing it.
7. **Close**: portability check (`python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`), commit by path in each repo touched, push, and add a line to `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md` (and the touched repo's own STATUS).

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).
- **Audit agents run on Sonnet (Eric, 2026-10-31).** When audits run as subagents, pass `model: "sonnet"`. Never Haiku. Parallel agents each edit only their own skill, commit by path, and never push; the main session updates this file and pushes once at the end.

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30; this five picked 2026-10-31.

| # | Skill | Runs (60 d) | Why it is on the list | Care |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `new-project` | 2 | Scaffolds a DEV project: repo, AGENTS.md, STATUS, private GitHub repo. | Creating a GitHub repo is outside-facing: test in a temp folder with no remote; a real repo waits for Eric. |
| 2 | `session-miner` | 2 | Mines recent sessions for uncaptured lessons and routes them to memory, vault or a skill. | Writes memory and vault notes: test with output to a temp folder; session logs may hold secrets (Tier A `session-history-tracked`). |
| 3 | `sports-science-research-grounding` | 2 | Zotero-first answers to sport-science questions; batch full-library runs. | Full-library batch is costly: test one question, never a batch unasked. |
| 4 | `claudex-loop` | 1 | Full plan-build-inspect loop with Codex; `codex-review` routes to its runner. | Vendored (`~/.agents/vendor-review/claudex-loop`, upstream remote only): commit locally, never push. Eric's local runner patch forces `gpt-6-astra` (config.toml says `gpt-6.1-terra`) at medium effort (raised from low 10-31, `ff24303`) and breaks one unit test; `runtime.md` still says omitting `--model`/`--effort` uses CLI config (10-31 codex-review audit). |
| 5 | `codex-build` | 1 | Codex builds a work order; Claude inspects the changes. | Same vendored repo as `claudex-loop`: commit locally, never push. |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

## Areas

| Area | Index | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |
| Performance | `PERFORMANCE.md` | Athlete monitoring, testing, load, risk. GPS, force plate, VALD, DEXA, S2. |
| Research | `RESEARCH.md` | Literature, Zotero, book library, reading pipelines. |
| Platform | `PLATFORM.md` | KeystoneOS, dashboards, CLIs, scheduled jobs. |
| Program | `PROGRAM.md` | Staff reporting, curriculum, proposals, vetting, brand. |
| Personal | `PERSONAL.md` | Side projects. Not Baylor work. |
| Commands | `COMMANDS.md` | Desk reference: every report/project command Eric can run himself. |
| Workflow | `WORKFLOW.md` | The ideal day, week and semester: which skill, mod and ritual, when and why. |
| Daily | `DAILY.md` | One-page daily checklist, sit down to sign off. Infographic `docs/DAILY-WORKFLOW.png`. |

## Elsewhere on disk

`~/DEV` in this file means the workspace root on the Mac. Machine paths are in `~/.claude/machine.md`.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/` | Parked projects. Not a git repo, so the consolidation sweep skips it. Has its own `README.md`. |
| `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | Loose files from the `~/DEV` root. Own repo. |
| SecondBrain vault | Obsidian vault, ~850 notes. Own `CLAUDE.md`. `~/SecondBrain`. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | ~45 skills (plugins add more) |
| `~/go/bin/` | ~8 custom CLIs built with `cli-printing-press` |
| `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/` | ~190 compiled articles |

## Cloud sessions

A cloud session (`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`) has only this repo cloned. No
project folders, no `~/.claude`, no Drive mount. Work this way instead:

- **Open a project by attaching its repo.** The GitHub repo name is the folder
  name in the area index (`Football/PFF_Data_Project/` → `erash11/PFF_Data_Project`).
  Exceptions: `Website/` → `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`; `DexaProject/` has no
  repo and is never opened from the cloud. Not in the map? List Eric's repos and
  ask which one before guessing.
- **Then follow that repo's Session routine** (read `docs/STATUS.md` first; commit
  and push at the end). Nothing pushed means nothing the other machine can see.
- **Documents:** use the Google Drive connector. The mount paths in this file are
  Mac only.
- **Skip what only exists on a machine:** `recall.py`, `memsearch`, Tier A memory files,
  SecondBrain, `~/go/bin` CLIs, local databases (DuckDB, `.rds`). If a task
  needs one of these, say so and suggest a local session on the Mac.
- **Health data stays out:** never pull DexaProject, `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES`,
  or any folder whose `CLAUDE.md` says "local only" into a cloud session.

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

- ~50 projects carry a substantive `CLAUDE.md` (the rest are `@AGENTS.md` pointers). Read it before working in one.

## Handling care

- `DexaProject/` holds identifiable health data. It lives on Google Drive, not in
  `~/DEV`: `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/DexaProject`

  See `PERFORMANCE.md`.
  Never paste its contents into chat, an artifact, or an external service.

## Keeping this true

When a file moves or a new project starts, **update the router in the same
turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

The counts above are approximate on purpose — they convey scale, not state, and
a `~` keeps ordinary growth from making this file wrong. Re-measure them only
when one is off by enough to change a decision. Counts last checked 2026-10-23.

Memory files named in these indexes (`project_*.md`, `user_*.md`) live in the
workspace's Tier A folder: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/`. They auto-load
only when cwd is the workspace root itself — from inside a sub-project, open them by path.

Search everything with `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/recall.py "<question>"` (plain code, ~1 s;
it opens the best file and prints the matching paragraphs; on a weak or no match it also prints
memsearch's meaning search, ~10 s). Bench: `~/.claude/scripts/recall-bench/results.md`.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).
- **Audit agents run on Sonnet (Eric, 2026-10-31).** When audits run as subagents, pass `model: "sonnet"`. Never Haiku. Parallel agents each edit only their own skill, commit by path, and never push; the main session updates this file and pushes once at the end.

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30; this five picked 2026-10-31.

| # | Skill | Runs (60 d) | Why it is on the list | Care |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `session-miner` | 2 | Mines recent sessions for uncaptured lessons and routes them to memory, vault or a skill. | Writes memory and vault notes: test with output to a temp folder; session logs may hold secrets (Tier A `session-history-tracked`). |

Eric's local runner patch forces `gpt-6.1-terra` at medium, matching config.toml (Eric 10-31; was astra/low) and breaks one unit test; `runtime.md` still says omitting `--model`/`--effort` uses CLI config (10-31 codex-review audit). |
| 3 | `codex-build` | 1 | Codex builds a work order; Claude inspects the changes. | Same vendored repo as `claudex-loop`: commit locally, never push. |
| 4 | `impeccable` | 1 | Frontend design skill: design, critique, polish, live browser iteration. | Large owned skill (58 files): audit SKILL.md and the files it routes to first; test a critique on a temp page, never a live site. |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.
4. **Fix**: real bugs first, then the writing-for-agents pass (steps in run order, a **Done when** line, positive rules, one home per fact, reference only some runs need moved to a sibling file). A script fix that adds a branch gets a small test.
5. **Test** by running the skill for real where it is safe. Data sent to an outside service (Jev, email, Teams) waits for Eric.
6. **Codex review**: `codex exec -s read-only "<prompt>" < /dev/null` on the diff (without `< /dev/null` it can wait on stdin forever), output to `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-<topic>-<date>.{md,txt}`. Check each finding before fixing it.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).

---
name: codex-review
description: "Codex as the independent reviewer of a plan or a code change (diff, branch, PR), run as a bounded review-fix-recheck loop with Claude coordinating. Use for /codex-review, 'have codex review this plan', or 'use codex to review the PR'. For the full plan-build-inspect loop, use claudex-loop."
---

# Codex Review

Codex reviews; this Claude session coordinates. It runs each round, checks every finding against the source, records a disposition, and stops at the round cap. Started inside Codex instead: same-provider review is not independent, so follow `claudex-loop` with Claude as the reviewer: its `review` mode for a plan, `inspect` for code.

The invocation authorizes reviewing and revising the plan. Change code only when the user already authorized that work.

## 1. Set up

- `RUNNER=~/.claude/skills/claudex-loop/scripts/runner.py`, the installed sibling skill, never a file in the target repo. `python3 "$RUNNER" roles --host claude` must print `"reviewer": "codex"`.
- `S="$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/codex-review"` (or the session scratchpad), then `mkdir -p "$S"`. It must sit outside the reviewed checkout: the runner refuses artifacts inside it. `$S` holds the brief, dispositions and `artifacts/`; it is the run log.
- Pick the mode by what is reviewed:

| Reviewed | Mode | `--plan` | Extra | Next round |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A plan file | `review` | the plan | none | `--resume` the last result |
| A code change: diff, branch, PR | `inspect` | a brief in `$S`: goal, PR link, focus areas, what counts as correct | `--base` = the commit before the change | a fresh `inspect` |

  For `inspect`, run from a checkout of the change. The reviewer gets the diff of tracked and staged changes against `--base`, plus a list of untracked files to read; ignored files are left out. For `--base`, use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>` for a branch or PR, `HEAD` for uncommitted work.
- Pass `--model` and `--effort` on every round. Without them the runner's local patch quietly uses `CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL` / `CODEX_REVIEW_EFFORT` (top of `runner.py`) and records the model as "CLI default (unresolved)". Use the user's choice, or those two constants.

## 2. Run a round

```text
python3 "$RUNNER" review  --host claude --repo REPO --plan PLAN       --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
python3 "$RUNNER" inspect --host claude --repo REPO --plan "$S/brief.md" --base BASE --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
```

A round can take up to the 600 s default timeout: run it in the background and wait for the notification. The first line of `roundN.out` names the round's artifact folder; a first line starting `claudex-loop:` is an error from before the run started (missing path, missing `--base`, rejected `--resume`). Read the folder's `result.json`: `status` must be `completed`, then read `response.verdict`, `response.summary` and `response.findings`. Exit code 0 means a completed turn, not approval.

## 3. Arbitrate, then loop

- **APPROVED**: done. Present any low-severity advice and the reviewer's `limitations`.
- **REVISE**: verify each finding against the code or plan before acting. Accept and fix it, or reject it with a reason. Write the dispositions to `$S/roundN-dispositions.md`, then run the next round with `--feedback` that file:
  - plan: `review ... --resume <this round's result.json>`, same model and effort (the runner refuses a mismatch);
  - code: a fresh `inspect` with the same `--base`, after the fixes are in the checkout.
- **BLOCKED, `status: failed`, or a malformed result**: this is not approval. Report the missing evidence or the `error` field and `stderr.txt`, and fix the cause before spending another round.

Stop at 5 completed rounds, or the user's `rounds` / `MAX_ROUNDS`. A REVISE on the last round ends the loop: report its findings, and list any fix made after it as unreviewed. An approved plan that will be built next gets `python3 "$RUNNER" check --host claude --repo REPO --plan PLAN --approval <approved result.json>`; building and inspecting the result belongs to `claudex-loop`, because a plan approval does not cover the code built from it.

Flags, sandbox boundaries and result validation: [runtime reference](../claudex-loop/references/runtime.md).

**Done when** the last completed round is APPROVED, the round cap is reached, or a BLOCKED or failed round needs the user to fix its cause; and the report gives: each finding with its disposition, unresolved findings with Claude's position, rounds used, the final `result.json` path, and the model and effort passed next to any model `result.json` observed.

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).
- **Audit agents run on Sonnet (Eric, 2026-10-31).** When audits run as subagents, pass `model: "sonnet"`. Never Haiku. Parallel agents each edit only their own skill, commit by path, and never push; the main session updates this file and pushes once at the end.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).

# Skill audit list

"The list" for skill audits. When Eric says "audit the next skill on the list", take the first row under **Next** and follow **Method**.

**Rules (Eric, 2026-10-30):**

- **Next always holds five.** When a skill's audit is done, in the same commit as the fix: move its row to **Done** (date, commits, headline), then refill **Next** with the top skill from `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/skill-audit-next.py` as the new last row (runs, why, care).
- **Done is final.** A skill in **Done** never returns to **Next**, unless Eric explicitly names it to be added back. Then move its row back to **Next** and note the date he asked. The script already skips every skill in either table.
- **Every audit runs `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents`.** Call it through the Skill tool at the start of each audit, and again for the review pass, even when it ran earlier in the session. Working from memory of it is the slip this rule exists for (the 10-30 meeting-sync audit missed six wording faults until the skill was called).
- **Audit agents run on Sonnet (Eric, 2026-10-31).** When audits run as subagents, pass `model: "sonnet"`. Never Haiku. Parallel agents each edit only their own skill, commit by path, and never push; the main session updates this file and pushes once at the end.

## Next

Ranked by real use: Skill-tool calls and typed `/commands` in the last 60 days of session logs, owned skills only (`skill-audit-next.py`). First five picked 2026-10-30; this five picked 2026-10-31.

| # | Skill | Runs (60 d) | Why it is on the list | Care |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | (empty) | | 2026-10-31: `skill-audit-next.py` prints nothing; every owned skill used in the last 60 days is audited. | Re-run the script before the next audit; a skill joins only once it is used. |

When the script prints nothing, every used skill has been audited: tell Eric, and keep **Next** shorter than five.

## Method

What "audit like we've been doing" means, in order:

1. **Load** `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` through the Skill tool (see Rules).
2. **Read** the skill, its other files, and the scripts and CLIs it calls. Find its callers (`grep -rn '<name>' ~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) and any scheduled job that does the same work.
3. **Verify every claim** against the real thing: paths exist, `--help` matches the flags, error codes and log lines exist in the script, the schedule matches the plist. Look at recent real runs (logs, outputs) for what actually went wrong.
4. **Fix**: real bugs first, then the writing-for-agents pass (steps in run order, a **Done when** line, positive rules, one home per fact, reference only some runs need moved to a sibling file). A script fix that adds a branch gets a small test.
5. **Test** by running the skill for real where it is safe. Data sent to an outside service (Jev, email, Teams) waits for Eric.
6. **Codex review**: `codex exec -s read-only "<prompt>" < /dev/null` on the diff (without `< /dev/null` it can wait on stdin forever), output to `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-<topic>-<date>.{md,txt}`. Check each finding before fixing it.
7. **Close**: portability check (`python3 ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/skill-portability-check.py`), commit by path in each repo touched, push, and add a line to `~/DEV/docs/STATUS.md` (and the touched repo's own STATUS).

content.content:
1. **Prior report** = the newest `*-status.md` in `{vault_status_reports}` (the folder also holds drafts,
   PDFs and HTML). Period start = its `period_end`; period end = today. With no prior record, start = 14
   days ago. Report number = prior `report_number` + 1.
2. **Missed fortnights widen the period.** The archive never has a gap.
3. **Sent or not.** A report counts as sent when its record says `sent: true` or its folder holds
   `YYYY-MM-DD-email-sent.txt`. When the prior report has neither, add "did report N go out?" to the
   Step 4 batch; an unconfirmed report stays unsent. If Eric says it never went out, period start = the `period_start` of the
   newest report that did, so its content folds into this one.
4. **Send dates** fall every 14 days from 2026-08-24 (the first send, "Starting these updates every two
   weeks"): 2026-11-02, 11-16, 11-30, 12-14. The last is 12-14; the semester closes 12-18.
   `python3 -c "import datetime as d;b=d.date(2026,8,24);t=d.date.today();print(next(b+d.timedelta(14*n) for n in range(40) if b+d.timedelta(14*n)>t))"`
   prints the next date after today. The footer's "Next report" is the grid date after this report's own.
5. KR 4.1 is eight reports through 2026-12-18. Step 8 states how many are confirmed sent.

**Done when** you hold period start and end, the report number, the prior report's sent state, and the next
send date.
-----

**Done when** one full pass leaves every box ticked. Show Eric the draft only then.

## Step 6 — Emit

Three files in `{vault_status_reports}`:

1. **`YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — plain text, only what gets pasted: from "Kenny, Coach Ruf," to "Eric".
   No markdown, no header block, no cut list; a select-all copy goes into Outlook with zero cleanup.
2. **`YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — copy `assets/one-pager.html` to `YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.html`, fill every
   `{{placeholder}}`, then run
   `python3 ~/.claude/skills/status-report/scripts/onepager_pdf.py render <html> <pdf>`
   (`python` on Windows). It measures first (budget 950px at 666px width) and refuses a file with
   placeholders left. Over budget, cut prose and keep the type at 9.6pt or larger. The page is a printed
   memorandum: single column, one serif family, letterspaced small-cap heads, one green hairline. Status
   dots, badges, bolded stat lines, progress bars and two-column grids stay out.
3. **`YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record in the template's Layer 3 shape, with frontmatter
   `report_number`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `next_send`, `sent: false`, `word_count`,
   `sources_degraded:`. Cuts and softened lines (what came out of the email, and why) go in a "Cut and
   softened" section; "Not for the report" stays candid.

Also print the email text in the reply.

**Never send, upload or share.** No Drive upload, no Teams post. The connected Gmail is Eric's personal address; create no Gmail draft. Eric sends from
Outlook on the work account, after he has read the report.

**Done when** all three files exist, the measure printed a height at or under 950, and the PDF is one page.

## Step 7 — Log

- Update `{canonical_projects}` with confirmed status, sport and KR.
- For each project reported as moved, run `/project update "<name>" "<note>"` (the `project` skill), and
  leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted.

**Done when** each moved project has an `updates[]` entry and the canonical list is current.

## Step 8 — Report to Eric

State: word count, report number, next send date, sports that appeared, anything the checks flagged, the
three file paths, and `N of D days logged` from the supervisor log, stated plainly ("6 of 14 days
logged, so the interview covered the other 8 from memory"). Add any stale-meeting or degraded-source note
from Step 2, and how many reports are confirmed sent toward KR 4.1's eight.

When this run hit a problem no Step 5 box covers, whether you caught it or Eric did while editing, end with
one proposed new checklist line and its reason. Add it to Step 5 on his yes.

### 11. The slate is retired (Eric, 2026-10-30)
Eric: "clear the project slate, that idea and process is not working for me." `meta.slate.retired`
is set and `meta.slate.cap` is null, so there is no job cap, no 7-day clock (`seven_day.check`
returns nothing, so closeout's `--apply` pauses nothing) and no `slate-check` prompt
(`slate.check` returns OK, disabled). Active job rows now follow Eric's own list of current work:
Athletics_Research_Council, NCAA_BestPractices_Doc, SoftwareTech_Review (his three for Kenny),
then Education_Curriculum, RTP_Constraints_Course, HPI_Protocol. Charters and checkpoints stay in
the data, unread. The board, the sweep and receivers are unchanged.

## Routine choices

- **Resume card (Q5 → A).** Four lines:
  - *What it is*: registry `purpose`, one line.
  - *Where it stands*: the last dated STATUS "Done" entry, or failing that the last registry
    update.
  - *Next step*: the first item of STATUS `## Next`, or `next_action` for Drive-only rows.
  - *Last touched*: from landed, either machine.

  The receiver is added per Decision 7. The full Next list and update history stay in the repo.
- **Starting rules carry over (Q9 → A).** The slate cap and the 7-day rule both stay. The
  board's Start runs the same checks as the terminal (same function, not a parallel browser
  path): it refuses over the cap and starts the 7-day clock. The 7-day countdown shows on the
  card. Revisit both rules at the 2026-12-18 checkpoint with real data.
-----
def week_report(data: dict, end: _dt.date) -> str:
    """Markdown summary of the 7 days ending `end`, for Eric's own weekly review.

    Written by the Friday ritual run into the vault. Blocks are updates whose
    note starts with "[block]" - interview-me logs them that way.
    """
    start = end - _dt.timedelta(days=6)
    lines = [f"# Weekly slate - week ending {end}", f"Window: {start} to {end}", ""]
    cfg = (data.get("meta") or {}).get("slate")
    if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
        lines.append("Slate not configured (meta.slate missing).")
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    result = check(data, end)
    lines += [f"**Slate:** {result['status']} - {result['active']} of {result['cap']} active", ""]
    active = sorted((p for p in data.get("projects", [])
                     if p.get("lane") == "job" and p.get("status") == "active"),
                    key=lambda p: p.get("rank", 0))
    for p in active:
        c = p.get("charter") or {}
        updates = sorted((u for u in p.get("updates") or [] if _in_window(u.get("date"), start, end)),
                         key=lambda u: u["date"])
        blocks = [u for u in updates if str(u.get("note", "")).startswith("[block]")]
        lines += [f"## {p['name']} - {c.get('receiver') or 'no receiver'}", "",
                  f"- Blocks logged: {len(blocks)}"]
        if updates:
            lines.append("- Moved:")
            lines += [f"  - {u['date']}: {u['note']}" for u in updates]
        else:
            lines.append("- No movement logged this week.")
        steps = c.get("steps") or []
        done = [s for s in steps if _in_window(s.get("done"), start, end)]
        if done:
            lines.append("- Steps done: " + "; ".join(s["name"] for s in done))
        # Same rule as check(): due today is not late yet.
        late = [s for s in steps if not s.get("done") and (parse_date(s.get("due")) or end) < end]
        for s in late:
            lines.append(f"- LATE: {s['name']} was due {s['due']}")

import datetime as dt

import slate

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
END = dt.date(2026, 9, 25)  # a Friday


def steps(done1=None):
    return [
        {"name": "Plan agreed with receiver", "due": "2026-09-18", "done": done1},
        {"name": "First draft to receiver", "due": "2026-10-16", "done": None},
        {"name": "Final delivered", "due": "2026-11-13", "done": None},
        {"name": "Receiver confirms in use", "due": "2026-12-11", "done": None},
    ]


def project(name, rank, updates=(), status="active", done1=None):
    return {
        "name": name, "lane": "job", "rank": rank, "status": status,
        "purpose": "p", "next_action": "n",
        "updates": list(updates),
        "charter": {"pillar": "data", "jd_duty": "d", "receiver": f"{name} receiver",
                    "done_means": "x", "finish_by": "2026-12-11", "steps": steps(done1)},
    }


def registry():
    return {
        "meta": {"slate": {
            "cap": 5, "semester_close": "2026-12-18", "next_up": ["Queued"],
            "checkpoints": [
                {"name": "Status report #3 sent", "due": "2026-09-25", "done": "2026-09-25"},
                {"name": "Status report #4 sent", "due": "2026-10-09", "done": None},
            ],
        }},
        "projects": [
            project("Beta", 2, updates=[
                {"date": "2026-09-19", "note": "[block] drafted outline"},   # day 1 of window
                {"date": "2026-09-18", "note": "[block] too old"},           # outside window

    def section(self, name):
        start = self.md.index(f"## {name}")
        nxt = self.md.find("\n## ", start + 1)
        return self.md[start: nxt if nxt != -1 else None]

    def test_title_and_window(self):
        self.assertIn("2026-09-19", self.md.splitlines()[0] + self.md.splitlines()[1])
        self.assertIn("2026-09-25", self.md.splitlines()[0])

    def test_active_projects_in_rank_order(self):
        self.assertLess(self.md.index("## Alpha"), self.md.index("## Beta"))

    def test_block_count_only_counts_blocks_in_window(self):
        self.assertIn("Blocks logged: 2", self.section("Alpha"))
