# Applied Performance — Prioritization Rules

**Why this exists.** "I would start one project, work a little on it, and start a new one because of a random idea or a suggestion. Nothing had a deadline. Done was never defined." — 2026-09-14. Four earlier fixes died because each had to be remembered. These rules are checked by a timer, not by memory.

## The four rules

**1. Active only with a charter.** A job project is active only when it has:
- **Pillar** — data, education, or research — and the JD duty it serves.
- **Receiver** — a named person who asked for it or agreed to receive it. *No name, not active.*
- **Done means** — one sentence: the thing handed over.
- **4 dated steps** — Plan agreed with receiver → First draft to receiver → Final delivered → Receiver confirms it is in use.
- **Finish date** — on or before semester close (2026-12-18).

**2. Four active, no more.** A new project starts only when one is finished or dropped. The one waiting for a slot is "next up." *Fall 2026 exception: cap is 5 so research keeps one project (decided 2026-09-14). Back to 4 in Spring 2027.*

**3. Ideas wait.** New ideas and suggestions go to `/project idea`. Flag an idea only if it has a pillar **and** a receiver. It still waits for a slot.

**4. The timer checks.** `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` runs `portfolio.py slate-check` and raises a desktop prompt when:
- more than 4 job projects are active,
- a step date passed and the step is not done,
- a project is past its finish date,
- the Oct 15 checkpoint or Dec 18 semester close was missed,
- an active project has no full charter,
- a slot is open and a project is waiting.

## Where things live

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The project list, charters, cap | `DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json` (`charter` per project, `meta.slate`) |
| The "why" — objectives and Fall KRs | [[Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27]] |
| Check now | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check` |
| Mark a step done | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done HPI_Protocol --step 1` |
| Mark a report sent | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done "report #2"` |
| Project time | One 2-hour calendar block per project per week, placed in open slots: Drive `05_SYSTEMS/ProjectBlocks/fall-2026-project-blocks.ics` |
| Log a block | `/interview-me` asks "which project block, what moved, step done?" (Part 0b) |
| Weekly report | Written every Friday by the timer: `Inbox/weekly-slate/YYYY-MM-DD.md` |
| Pulse to Chris + Kenny | Biweekly status report — Shipped comes from finished steps |

## When a step slips

Do one of three things the same week: **do it**, **re-date it with the receiver** (tell them), or **drop the project** and free the slot. Silent slipping is the only wrong answer.

## Retired

- `okr-tracker/` — frozen since 2026-06-12, still the June KR set.
- The Thursday unit check-in from the v2 playbook — it needed Blake.

# Applied Performance — Prioritization Rules

> **Retired 2026-10-30.** Eric: "clear the project slate, that idea and process is not working for me." No job cap, no charter gate, no 7-day clock, no `slate-check` prompt (project-triage design Decision 11). Active job projects follow Eric's own list of current work on the board. Rule 3 still holds in a new form: ideas go to `/project idea` and wait as cards in the board's Inbox. The rules below are kept as history.

**Why this exists.** "I would start one project, work a little on it, and start a new one because of a random idea or a suggestion. Nothing had a deadline. Done was never defined." — 2026-09-14. Four earlier fixes died because each had to be remembered. These rules are checked by a timer, not by memory.

## The four rules

**1. Active only with a charter.** A job project is active only when it has:
- **Pillar** — data, education, or research — and the JD duty it serves.
- **Receiver** — a named person who asked for it or agreed to receive it. *No name, not active.*
- **Done means** — one sentence: the thing handed over.
- **4 dated steps** — Plan agreed with receiver → First draft to receiver → Final delivered → Receiver confirms it is in use.
- **Finish date** — on or before semester close (2026-12-18).

**2. Four active, no more.** A new project starts only when one is finished or dropped. The one waiting for a slot is "next up." *Fall 2026 exception: cap is 5 so research keeps one project (decided 2026-09-14). Back to 4 in Spring 2027.*

**3. Ideas wait.** New ideas and suggestions go to `/project idea`. Flag an idea only if it has a pillar **and** a receiver. It still waits for a slot.

**4. The timer checks.** `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` runs `portfolio.py slate-check` and raises a desktop prompt when:
- more than 4 job projects are active,
- a step date passed and the step is not done,
- a project is past its finish date,
- the Oct 15 checkpoint or Dec 18 semester close was missed,
- an active project has no full charter,
- a slot is open and a project is waiting.

## Where things live

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The project list, charters, cap | `DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json` (`charter` per project, `meta.slate`) |
| The "why" — objectives and Fall KRs | [[Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27]] |
| Check now | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check` |
| Mark a step done | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done HPI_Protocol --step 1` |
| Mark a report sent | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done "report #2"` |
| Project time | One 2-hour calendar block per project per week, placed in open slots: Drive `05_SYSTEMS/ProjectBlocks/fall-2026-project-blocks.ics` |
| Log a block | `/interview-me` asks "which project block, what moved, step done?" (Part 0b) |
| Weekly report | Written every Friday by the timer: `Inbox/weekly-slate/YYYY-MM-DD.md` |
| Pulse to Chris + Kenny | Biweekly status report — Shipped comes from finished steps |

## When a step slips

Do one of three things the same week: **do it**, **re-date it with the receiver** (tell them), or **drop the project** and free the slot. Silent slipping is the only wrong answer.

## Retired

- `okr-tracker/` — frozen since 2026-06-12, still the June KR set.
- The Thursday unit check-in from the v2 playbook — it needed Blake.

Three layers, one pass.

Do not merge the layers. The email is short because short gets read. The PDF exists so
the short version doesn't cost you credit. The internal file exists so the whole thing
doubles as your time-and-effort documentation without bloating what Chris reads.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny should finish the email knowing what moved,
what needs them, and what is at risk. **Secondary job: credit** — specifically for work
across sports beyond football and basketball. The sport tags and the coverage panel are
not decoration; they are the reason this report exists.

## LAYER 1 — THE EMAIL BODY

---

## LAYER 2 — THE PDF ONE-PAGER

Built from `assets/one-pager.html`, rendered via the `html-to-pdf` skill. One page, no
exceptions — if it runs to two, cut, don't shrink the type.

Contents, in order:

1. **Header** — "Applied Performance — Status" · period dates · prepared by Eric Rash ·
   To: Chris Ruf, Cc: Kenny Boyd.
2. **The five sections**, same content as the email, with room for the detail the word
   ceiling cut.
3. **Sport coverage panel** — the reason the attachment exists.

   | Sport | Touched this period | What was delivered |
   |---|---|---|

   List every sport the department serves, including the ones with nothing this period.
   A blank row is information: it shows Chris and Kenny where coverage is thin, which is
   a more honest and more useful artifact than a list of only the sports you worked.
   Over a semester the accumulated panels are the evidence of breadth — that is the
   defensibility layer, and it works because it was never padded.

4. **KR progress strip** — the 14 KRs from `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` (v3)
   with status, one line. Read `okr-tracker/SCOREBOARD.md` for live confidence values.
   Never read the cadence doc's KR table — it is the superseded v2 set of 9.
5. **Footer** — report N of the cycle, next report date.

---

## LAYER 3 — THE INTERNAL RECORD

Written to `SecondBrain/Inbox/status-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`. Never sent. This is
the answer to "documentation of how I'm spending my time" — it accrues without costing
the email its readability.

```markdown
---
type: status-report
period_start: YYYY-MM-DD
period_end: YYYY-MM-DD
report_number: N
sent_to: [Chris Ruf]
cc: [Kenny Boyd]
sent: false
meetings_held: 0
sports_touched: []
email_word_count: 0
---

## Email as sent
<exact Layer 1 text, for the archive>

## Meetings held
| Date | Meeting | With | What came out of it | Surfaced in report? |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Conversations (not meetings)
Hallway, text, sideline, phone — the ones no transcript caught. These are invisible to
every automated source, which makes them the highest-value thing the interview captures.
- {{who}} — {{what}} — {{surface it, or let it sit?}}

## Ideas generated
- {{idea}} — {{what triggered it}} — {{park / pitch / build}}

## Full active project roster
Every job-lane project, including ones too small for the email.
| Project | KR | Sport | Moved? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## KR ledger
| KR | Owner | Status | Moved this period |
|---|---|---|---|

## Not for the report
Candid notes — frustrations, politics, half-formed reads on people and direction.
This is why the internal file exists. Keep somewhere to be honest.
```

## Cadence

**Twice monthly — 1st and 3rd Friday**, from September onward.

> **Assumption, flagged for veto.** You said "twice a month, not every two weeks," then
> "every two weeks" a paragraph later. 1st-and-3rd-Friday is my pick, not yours: it's
> twice monthly as asked, lands on fixed weekdays so it's predictable for Chris, and
> never produces the three-report month that a true 14-day cycle does. Say the word and
> it becomes strict biweekly instead. Worth settling before the second send, because
> after that the cadence is set by precedent rather than by decision.

**Exception through Aug 31:** KR 4.1 requires ≥3 reports sent by Aug 31 and none exist
yet. Twice-monthly cannot get there. Run **weekly — Aug 14, Aug 21, Aug 28** — to clear
the KR, then settle into twice-monthly on Sep 5.

The report covers the period since the previous report, not a fixed calendar window. A
missed send widens the next period rather than skipping it — the archive stays gap-free,
which is what makes it usable as a time record.

with no Key Result and no sport is hard to justify in a status report.

=== feedback_admin-docs-house-style
name: admin-docs-house-style
description: Every document going to administration uses the Baylor house style (Baylor_Doc_Style) — no local sizes/margins; ask before breaking a page limit
metadata:

Every document going to Baylor Athletics administration (leadership, admin, Kenny Boyd,
Chris Ruf) is built with the house style in `~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`
(`baylor_docstyle.py`, `BaylorDoc`; exemplar is the Software & Technology Management
Framework draft, chosen 2026-08-30). Use only its components (`section`, `table`, `note`,
`para`, `bullets`) and its defaults: Calibri 10.5, 9.5pt tables, 0.80/0.90in margins.
No local font sizes, margins, Normal-style overrides or hand-built tables.

**Why:** on 2026-09-29 I shrank the Tech Inventory by-unit list (7.5pt, 0.6in margins,
custom table) to force one page. Eric: "the docs should have the same baylor styling
we've been using in other documentation. make a note that future docs going to
administration should use it also." When asked, he chose two pages in house style over
one page that broke it.

**How to apply:** if content won't fit a page limit in house style, ask Eric (more pages,
or cut content) instead of shrinking below house sizes. Word COM is the page-count
authority (`doc_platform.word_pdf` in Tech_Inventory_Analysis). Related:
[[tech-inventory-refresh]], [[kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences]],
[[baylor-department-names]].
=== project_kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences
name: kenny-boyd-doc-review-preferences
description: "Kenny Boyd's editorial constraints on Athletics policy/framework docs — no language implying past incompetence, no judgmental tier labels, name the seniority of reviewers"
metadata: 

Kenny Boyd (reviewer on the Baylor Athletics Software and Technology Management
Framework) consistently pushes back on three things in draft policy language:

1. **No language that implies the department was previously incompetent.** He cut
   "so the department stops discovering it is in the final year of an agreement
   with no time to act" for exactly this reason. Rewrite as forward-looking
   capability ("advance visibility of contract end dates and the lead time to
   evaluate options"), not as a problem being fixed.
2. **No judgmental or ranking-flavored labels.** He rejected the Light / Standard /
   Elevated review tiers. Neutral, descriptive, escalating names work better —
   Level 1 Standard / Level 2 Enhanced / Level 3 Comprehensive Review. He floated
   Basic / Intermediate / Advanced, which reads as sophistication of the
   *technology* rather than depth of *review*.
3. **Name the seniority of the reviewer, not just the office.** For ITS he wanted
   it clear that a supervisory-level person with authority to commit resources is
   involved, not a line technician. Frame this as decision authority the request
   requires, never as competence of the staff.

He also wants Baylor branding carried through headers/footers and draft status
marked on every page.

Format (his own words, Tech Sync 2026-10-28): no long wordy documents; "economy of
words"; a clean cover with the details behind it; charts and trend lines over
text ("not a pre-K version" either). Say plainly when something already exists
("we already have this") so work is not duplicated. To him "the SOP" means the
Software and Technology Management Framework.
=== user_baylor-department-names
name: baylor-department-names
description: "Baylor Athletics department names Eric uses; never write strength and conditioning, sports medicine, or sport science in his deliverables"
metadata: 

Baylor Athletics staff use these department names, and Eric corrects the generic ones (2026-09-16):

- **Athletic Performance**, not "strength and conditioning" / S&C
- **Athletic Medicine**, not "sports medicine"
- **Applied Performance**, not "sport science" / sports science (also Eric's own department)

**Why:** deliverables go to Baylor staff and leadership; generic industry names read as outside-written.
**How to apply:** use these names in any staff-facing deck, email, report, or role list. Weekly_Research_Review enforces them in `tools/build.js` (ROLES list). Related: [[prioritization-slate]].

[Normal] Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory
[Normal] Executive Summary
[Normal] 1. In Short
[Normal] All 32 units completed a five-question survey naming the technology they use, describing 190 distinct products across 52 submissions. The technology each unit uses is listed in Appendix A, Technology by unit. Appendix B lists every product by name, and Appendix C lists the products discontinued in the last 12 months.
[Normal] 2. The Inventory
[Normal] “Likely involve athlete information” counts every product in these categories: Video and analytics (28), Performance (18), Medical (12), Recruiting (8), Academic (5), Athlete management (4) and Athlete stipend (1).
[Normal] 3. Takeaways
[List Bullet] Most products have a single user. 132 of the 190 products were named by only one unit each, spread across 26 different units.
[List Bullet] Only two systems are department-wide. Teamworks and Microsoft Office are provided to all 32 units; the next most widely shared, Adobe Creative Suite, is used by 10.
[List Bullet] 9 products were retired in the last year. What each vendor still holds was not asked on the short form.
[List Bullet] 76 of the 190 products likely involve athlete information.
[Normal] Appendix A: Technology by unit
[Normal] Compiled from a department-wide survey of all 32 units, as of October 1, 2026. Teamworks and Microsoft Office are department-provided and listed for every unit. Products the Business Office purchases on behalf of other units are listed under the unit that uses them.
[Normal] Sports
[Normal] * Also listed by a performance or sports-medicine unit (Applied Performance, Athletics Performance or Athletic Medicine). The team may use it through that unit's staff rather than hold its own license.
[Normal] Support units
[Normal] Appendix B: Technology in use (190 products)
[Normal] Inventory as of October 1, 2026, compiled from unit responses. Alphabetical. Bold marks products named by three or more units; the unit count follows products named by more than one.

# Baylor Doc Style

The house look for Baylor Athletics Word documents, defined once.

`baylor_docstyle.py` is a single module. Document builders import it instead of
setting their own fonts, colours and spacing, so every document comes out
looking like the same department wrote it.

## Where the style comes from

Every measurement in the module was read out of:

```
~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/
    Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx
```

Eric chose that document as the house look on 2026-08-30. Nothing in the module
is invented. **If the module and that document ever disagree, the document
wins** — re-measure it rather than adjusting to taste.

## When to use it

**Every document going to administration** (leadership, Kenny Boyd, Chris Ruf,
senior staff) is built with this module, using only its components and defaults
— no local font sizes, margins or hand-built tables (Eric, 2026-09-29). If the
content will not fit a page limit in house style, ask Eric whether to add pages
or cut content; do not shrink below the house sizes.

## Use

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

d = BaylorDoc("Athletics Technology Inventory",
              deck="What the department runs, and who runs it.",
              status="Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026")

d.meta([["Status", "Interim"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance"]])
d.callout("Two deadlines, not one", "29 August was our own deadline...")
d.section("Coverage — who has responded")     # numbered automatically
d.subhead("Still outstanding")
d.para("Five units have yet to respond.")
d.bullets(["**Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed."])
d.numbered(["**Follow up with five units.** Golf (M), Tennis (M)..."])
d.quote("Everything we have has gone through ITS approval.")
d.table(["Unit", "Responses"], [["Football", 3]], numeric_cols=(1,))
d.note("A caveat, in small italic grey.")
d.small("A caption under a table.")
d.save("out.docx")
```

`**double asterisks**` mark inline bold in every text argument.

Section numbers are handed out in order, so inserting a section never means
renumbering the ones after it.

## What the style is

| Element | Setting |
|---|---|
| Page | Letter, margins 0.80in top/bottom, 0.90in left/right |
| Body | Calibri 10.5pt, 6pt after, line spacing 1.079 |
| Eyebrow | 9pt bold, gold `#B8860B` |
| Title | 19pt bold, Baylor green `#154734` |
| Deck | 11pt italic, grey `#595959` |
| Meta block | borderless label/value, 9pt |
| Callout | cream `#FFF4DA` box, 9.5pt, green heading |
| Section | numbered, 13pt bold green, green rule under |
| Subhead | 11.5pt bold green |
| Table | green header band, white header text, 9.5pt body |
| Footer | centred 7.5pt grey — title, status, "Baylor Athletics", page number |
| Header | none |

## Three things not to change

**Calibri, everywhere.** The exemplar sets no font on any run, so every size
inherits Normal. Calibri ships with Office, which is why the document survives

    """Export the PDF through Word and return Word's page count.

class BaylorDoc:
    """A Word document in the house style.

    Call the content methods in reading order and then save(). Section numbers
    are handed out automatically, so inserting a section never means renumbering
    the ones after it.
    """

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None,
                 eyebrow=EYEBROW_DEFAULT, footer_suffix="Baylor Athletics",
                 page_numbers=True):
        self.doc = Document()
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self._section_no = 0
        self._base_style()
        self._page_setup()
        self._footer(footer_suffix, page_numbers)
        self._title_block(title, deck, eyebrow)

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_style(self):
        st = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        st.font.name = BODY_FONT
        st.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(BODY_AFTER)
        st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = LINE_SPACING

    def _page_setup(self):
        sec = self.doc.sections[0]
        sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"])
        sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"])
        sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"])
        sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"])
        self.text_width = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"]

    def _footer(self, suffix, page_numbers):
        """Centred, quiet, and carrying the document's status on every page."""
        fp = self.doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        parts = [self.title]
        if self.status:
            parts.append(self.status)
        parts.append(suffix)
        r = fp.add_run("   ·   ".join(parts))
        r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
        if page_numbers:
            r2 = fp.add_run("   ·   ")
            r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(7.5)
            r2.font.color.rgb = GREY
            page_field(fp)

    def _title_block(self, title, deck, eyebrow):
        if eyebrow:
            p = self._p(space_after=1)
            add_runs(p, eyebrow, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
        p = self._p(space_after=2)
        add_runs(p, title, size=19, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        if deck:
            p = self._p(space_after=10)
            add_runs(p, deck, size=11, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def _p(self, space_before=None, space_after=None, style=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else self.doc.add_paragraph()
        if space_before is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        if space_after is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        return p

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Athletic Director brief of the technology inventory.

Run:
    uv run --with python-docx --with matplotlib python3 scripts/build_ad_brief.py

Why: Eric, 2026-10-31. KR 1.1 was met on 2026-10-01 (final documents to Kenny Boyd).
Per Eric's conversation with Kenny, a polished version goes to Doug McNamee, the
Athletic Director. Kenny's format (Tech Sync 2026-10-28): economy of words, a clean
cover with the details behind it, charts over text.

Shape: page 1 is the cover (numbers, takeaways, what comes next); page 2 is two
charts. The details behind it are the companion, deliverables/_SEND/Baylor Athletics
Technology Inventory.docx (Eric's 10-19 edit, after the 10-12 confirmation pass).

Every number is read from that companion's tables, so the brief cannot drift from
the document it points to. House style: Baylor_Doc_Style (admin docs rule). The
module has no chart component, so the charts are images in house colours placed
between house-style paragraphs; fonts, margins and tables stay at house defaults.
"""

import collections
import datetime
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

import docx
from docx.shared import Inches

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import doc_platform  # noqa: E402

doc_platform.add_doc_style_to_path()
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

COMPANION = os.path.join(REPO, "deliverables", "_SEND", "Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory.docx")
AS_OF = "October 1, 2026"
# Categories the companion counts as "likely involve athlete information" (its section 2).
ATHLETE = ["Video and analytics", "Performance", "Medical", "Recruiting", "Academic",
           "Athlete management", "Athlete stipend"]
GREEN, GOLD, GREY, LIGHT = "#154734", "#B8860B", "#595959", "#B9C4BF"


def read_companion(path):
    """Products (name, units, category, type) and the 32 unit rows, from the companion's tables."""
    d = docx.Document(path)
    by_header = {tuple(c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells): t for t in d.tables}
    products = []
    for t in d.tables:
        head = [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells]
        if head == ["Name", "Category", "Type"]:
            for r in t.rows[1:]:
                name, cat, typ = (c.text.strip() for c in r.cells)
                m = re.search(r"\((\d+) units\)", name)
                products.append((re.sub(r" \(\d+ units\)", "", name), int(m.group(1)) if m else 1, cat, typ))
    units = [r for t in d.tables if [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells] == ["Unit", "Software", "Hardware"]
             for r in t.rows[1:]]
    retired = [t for t in d.tables if [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells] == ["Name", "Unit", "Type"]]
    n_retired = len(retired[0].rows) - 1 if retired else None
    del by_header
    return products, len(units), n_retired


def figures(products, n_units, n_retired):
    cat = collections.Counter(p[2] for p in products)
    single = [p for p in products if p[1] == 1]
    f = {
        "units": n_units,
        "products": len(products),
        "software": sum(1 for p in products if p[3] == "Software"),
        "hardware": sum(1 for p in products if p[3] == "Hardware"),
        "athlete": sum(cat[c] for c in ATHLETE),
        "single": len(single),
        "everywhere": sorted(p[0] for p in products if p[1] == n_units),
        "next_shared": max((p for p in products if p[1] < n_units), key=lambda p: p[1]),
        "retired": n_retired,
        "cat": cat,
        "share": [("1 unit", len(single)),
                  ("2 units", sum(1 for p in products if p[1] == 2)),
                  ("3 to 10 units", sum(1 for p in products if 3 <= p[1] < n_units)),
                  (f"All {n_units} units", sum(1 for p in products if p[1] == n_units))],
    }
    # The four sharing bands must account for every product.
    assert sum(n for _, n in f["share"]) == f["products"], f["share"]
    assert f["athlete"] == sum(cat[c] for c in ATHLETE)
    return f


def charts(f, out_dir):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 9,
                         "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
                         "axes.edgecolor": GREY, "xtick.color": GREY, "ytick.color": "#222222"})
    paths = []

    # 1. Products by category; athlete-information categories in green.
    items = [(c, n) for c, n in f["cat"].most_common() if c != "Being confirmed"]
    other = f["cat"].get("Being confirmed", 0)
    items = items[::-1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.7, 3.55), dpi=200)
    colors = [GREEN if c in ATHLETE else LIGHT for c, _ in items]
    ax.barh([c for c, _ in items], [n for _, n in items], color=colors, height=0.68)
    for i, (_, n) in enumerate(items):
        ax.text(n + 0.4, i, str(n), va="center", fontsize=8, color="#222222")
    ax.set_xlabel("Products", color=GREY)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(n for _, n in items) * 1.12)
    from matplotlib.patches import Patch
    ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=GREEN, label=f"Likely involve athlete information ({f['athlete']})"),
                       Patch(color=LIGHT, label="Other")],
              loc="lower right", frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    p1 = os.path.join(out_dir, "ad_brief_categories.png"); fig.savefig(p1); plt.close(fig); paths.append(p1)

    # 2. How widely each product is shared.
    labels = [l for l, _ in f["share"]]; vals = [n for _, n in f["share"]]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.7, 2.05), dpi=200)
    ax.bar(labels, vals, color=[LIGHT, LIGHT, LIGHT, GREEN], width=0.6)
    for i, n in enumerate(vals):
        ax.text(i, n + 2, str(n), ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color="#222222")
    ax.set_ylabel("Products", color=GREY)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(vals) * 1.18)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)
    fig.tight_layout()
    p2 = os.path.join(out_dir, "ad_brief_sharing.png"); fig.savefig(p2); plt.close(fig); paths.append(p2)
    return paths, other


def build(f, chart_paths, other, out_docx):
    d = BaylorDoc("Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory",
                  deck="What technology the department uses, across all 32 units.",
                  status=f"Data as of {AS_OF}")
    d.meta([["Prepared for", "Doug McNamee, Director of Athletics"],
            ["Prepared by", "Eric Rash, Applied Performance, with Kenny Boyd"],
            ["Source", f"Survey of all {f['units']} units (sports and support units), closed September 29, 2026"]])

    d.section("In short")
    d.para(f"Every unit in the department answered a short survey about the technology it uses. "
           f"Together they named **{f['products']} distinct products** ({f['software']} software, "
           f"{f['hardware']} hardware). The full list, by unit and by product, is in the companion "
           f"document, *Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory*.")
    nxt = f["next_shared"]
    d.table(["Measure", f"As of {AS_OF}"], [
        ["Units responding", f"{f['units']} of {f['units']}"],
        ["Distinct products in use", str(f["products"])],
        ["Used by every unit", " and ".join(f["everywhere"])],
        ["Products used by one unit only", str(f["single"])],
        ["Products that likely involve athlete information", str(f["athlete"])],
        ["Products retired in the last 12 months", str(f["retired"])],
    ], widths=[3.6, 3.1])

    d.section("What it shows")
    d.bullets([
        f"**Two systems serve every unit:** {' and '.join(f['everywhere'])}. The next most widely "
        f"used, {nxt[0]}, is in {nxt[1]} units.",
        f"**Most technology is specific to one unit.** {f['single']} of the {f['products']} products are "
        f"used by a single unit, which reflects each sport's own needs.",
        f"**{f['athlete']} products likely involve athlete information** (video and analytics, "
        f"performance, medical, recruiting, academic and athlete management). These are where data "
        f"privacy and contract terms matter most.",
        f"**{f['retired']} products were retired in the last year.**",
    ])

    d.section("What comes next")
    d.bullets([
        "**Cost and contract terms.** With the Business Office: annual cost, renewal date and notice "
        "period for each product, ahead of the FY28 budget cycle.",
        "**New requests.** The Software and Technology Management Framework (in draft, with Kenny Boyd) "
        "sets how a unit requests and reviews new technology, so this inventory stays current.",
    ])

    d.page_break()
    d.section("The inventory at a glance")
    d.subhead("Products by category")
    d.doc.add_picture(chart_paths[0], width=Inches(d.text_width))
    note = f" {other} products are still being categorized and are not shown." if other else ""
    d.small(f"Green: the categories counted as likely involving athlete information.{note}")
    d.subhead("How widely each product is used")
    d.doc.add_picture(chart_paths[1], width=Inches(d.text_width))
    d.small(f"Number of units using each product. {f['single']} of {f['products']} are used by one unit; "
            f"{' and '.join(f['everywhere'])} are used by all {f['units']}.")
    d.save(out_docx)
    return out_docx


def word_pdf_sandboxed(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Word for Mac stalls on a hidden permission dialog when it saves outside its container
    (Tier A memory m365-agent-access), so export inside the container and copy the PDF out."""
    if sys.platform != "darwin":
        return doc_platform.word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    box = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Word/Data/tmp")
    os.makedirs(box, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_docx = os.path.join(box, os.path.basename(docx_path))
    tmp_pdf = os.path.join(box, os.path.basename(pdf_path))
    shutil.copy2(docx_path, tmp_docx)
    pages = doc_platform.word_pdf(tmp_docx, tmp_pdf)
    if pages is not None and os.path.exists(tmp_pdf):
        shutil.copy2(tmp_pdf, pdf_path)
    return pages


def main():
    out_dir = os.path.join(REPO, "deliverables")
    stem = f"Tech_Inventory_AD_BRIEF_ER_{datetime.date.today().isoformat()}"
    doc_platform.refuse_overwrite(stem, out_dir)
    products, n_units, n_retired = read_companion(COMPANION)
    f = figures(products, n_units, n_retired)
    build_dir = os.path.join(REPO, "build"); os.makedirs(build_dir, exist_ok=True)
    chart_paths, other = charts(f, build_dir)
    out_docx = build(f, chart_paths, other, os.path.join(out_dir, stem + ".docx"))
    pages = word_pdf_sandboxed(out_docx, os.path.join(out_dir, stem + ".pdf"))
    print(f"wrote {out_docx}")
    print(f"Word pages: {pages if pages is not None else 'Word not driven; no PDF'}")
    print({k: v for k, v in f.items() if k not in ("cat",)})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Athletic Director brief of the technology inventory.

Run:
    uv run --with python-docx --with matplotlib python3 scripts/build_ad_brief.py

Why: Eric, 2026-10-31. KR 1.1 was met on 2026-10-01 (final documents to Kenny Boyd).
Per Eric's conversation with Kenny, a polished version goes to Doug McNamee, the
Athletic Director. Kenny's format (Tech Sync 2026-10-28): economy of words, a clean
cover with the details behind it, charts over text.

Shape: page 1 is the cover (numbers, takeaways, what comes next); page 2 is two
charts. The details behind it are the companion, deliverables/_SEND/Baylor Athletics
Technology Inventory.docx (Eric's 10-19 edit, after the 10-12 confirmation pass).

Every number is read from that companion's tables, so the brief cannot drift from
the document it points to. House style: Baylor_Doc_Style (admin docs rule). The
module has no chart component, so the charts are images in house colours placed
between house-style paragraphs; fonts, margins and tables stay at house defaults.
"""

import collections
import datetime
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

import docx
from docx.shared import Inches

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
import doc_platform  # noqa: E402

doc_platform.add_doc_style_to_path()
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

COMPANION = os.path.join(REPO, "deliverables", "_SEND", "Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory.docx")
AS_OF = "October 1, 2026"
# Categories the companion counts as "likely involve athlete information" (its section 2).
ATHLETE = ["Video and analytics", "Performance", "Medical", "Recruiting", "Academic",
           "Athlete management", "Athlete stipend"]
GREEN, GOLD, GREY, LIGHT = "#154734", "#B8860B", "#595959", "#B9C4BF"


def read_companion(path):
    """Products (name, units, category, type) and the 32 unit rows, from the companion's tables."""
    d = docx.Document(path)
    by_header = {tuple(c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells): t for t in d.tables}
    products = []
    for t in d.tables:
        head = [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells]
        if head == ["Name", "Category", "Type"]:
            for r in t.rows[1:]:
                name, cat, typ = (c.text.strip() for c in r.cells)
                m = re.search(r"\((\d+) units\)", name)
                products.append((re.sub(r" \(\d+ units\)", "", name), int(m.group(1)) if m else 1, cat, typ))
    units = [r for t in d.tables if [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells] == ["Unit", "Software", "Hardware"]
             for r in t.rows[1:]]
    retired = [t for t in d.tables if [c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells] == ["Name", "Unit", "Type"]]
    n_retired = len(retired[0].rows) - 1 if retired else None
    del by_header
    return products, len(units), n_retired


def figures(products, n_units, n_retired):
    cat = collections.Counter(p[2] for p in products)
    single = [p for p in products if p[1] == 1]
    f = {
        "units": n_units,
        "products": len(products),
        "software": sum(1 for p in products if p[3] == "Software"),
        "hardware": sum(1 for p in products if p[3] == "Hardware"),
        "athlete": sum(cat[c] for c in ATHLETE),
        "single": len(single),
        "everywhere": sorted(p[0] for p in products if p[1] == n_units),
        "next_shared": max((p for p in products if p[1] < n_units), key=lambda p: p[1]),
        "retired": n_retired,
        "cat": cat,
        "share": [("1 unit", len(single)),
                  ("2 units", sum(1 for p in products if p[1] == 2)),
                  ("3 to 10 units", sum(1 for p in products if 3 <= p[1] < n_units)),
                  (f"All {n_units} units", sum(1 for p in products if p[1] == n_units))],
    }

    return f


def charts(f, out_dir):

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

                         "axes.edgecolor": GREY, "xtick.color": GREY, "ytick.color": "#222222"})
    paths = []

    other = f["cat"].get("Being confirmed", 0)
    items = items[::-1]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.7, 3.55), dpi=200)
    colors = [GREEN if c in ATHLETE else LIGHT for c, _ in items]
    ax.barh([c for c, _ in items], [n for _, n in items], color=colors, height=0.68)
    for i, (_, n) in enumerate(items):
        ax.text(n + 0.4, i, str(n), va="center", fontsize=8, color="#222222")
    ax.set_xlabel("Products", color=GREY)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    ax.set_xlim(0, max(n for _, n in items) * 1.12)
    from matplotlib.patches import Patch
    ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=GREEN, label=f"Likely involve athlete information ({f['athlete']})"),
                       Patch(color=LIGHT, label="Other")],
              loc="lower right", frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    p1 = os.path.join(out_dir, "ad_brief_categories.png"); fig.savefig(p1); plt.close(fig); paths.append(p1)

    # 2. How widely each product is shared.
    labels = [l for l, _ in f["share"]]; vals = [n for _, n in f["share"]]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.7, 2.05), dpi=200)
    ax.bar(labels, vals, color=[LIGHT, LIGHT, LIGHT, GREEN], width=0.6)
    for i, n in enumerate(vals):
        ax.text(i, n + 2, str(n), ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color="#222222")
    ax.set_ylabel("Products", color=GREY)
    ax.set_ylim(0, max(vals) * 1.18)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)
    fig.tight_layout()
    p2 = os.path.join(out_dir, "ad_brief_sharing.png"); fig.savefig(p2); plt.close(fig); paths.append(p2)
    return paths, other

return out_docx


def word_pdf_sandboxed(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Word for Mac stalls on a hidden permission dialog when it saves outside its container
    (Tier A memory m365-agent-access), so export inside the container and copy the PDF out."""
    if sys.platform != "darwin":
        return doc_platform.word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    # Word opens the .docx where it is; only its save goes into its own container.
    # (The shell may not write into the container: macOS blocks it.)
    box = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/Containers/com.microsoft.Word/Data/tmp")
    tmp_pdf = os.path.join(box, os.path.basename(pdf_path))
    pages = doc_platform.word_pdf(docx_path, tmp_pdf)
    if pages is not None and os.path.exists(tmp_pdf):
        shutil.copy2(tmp_pdf, pdf_path)
    return pages


def main():
    out_dir = os.path.join(REPO, "deliverables")
    stem = f"Tech_Inventory_AD_BRIEF_ER_{datetime.date.today().isoformat()}"
    doc_platform.refuse_overwrite(stem, out_dir)
    products, n_units, n_retired = read_companion(COMPANION)
    f = figures(products, n_units, n_retired)
    import tempfile
    build_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ad_brief_")   # chart PNGs are embedded in the .docx
    chart_paths, other = charts(f, build_dir)
    out_docx = build(f, chart_paths, other, os.path.join(out_dir, stem + ".docx"))
    pages = word_pdf_sandboxed(out_docx, os.path.join(out_dir, stem + ".pdf"))
    print(f"wrote {out_docx}")
    print(f"Word pages: {pages if pages is not None else 'Word not driven; no PDF'}")
    print({k: v for k, v in f.items() if k not in ("cat",)})

# Where Was I

Wraps one script. The script does the work; this skill says how to read it.

## Run it

```bash
python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py            # projects touched in the last 14 days
python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --days 3   # after a weekend
python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --days 7   # after a longer gap
python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --all      # every project with a STATUS.md
```

The script stays at `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py`. `closeout`, `dev-sync` and `startup` call that path. Do not move it.

## Read the output

- Each block is one repo: date STATUS.md was last committed, repo name, then `NEXT:`.
- `NEXT:` is the first item under `## Next` in that repo's `docs/STATUS.md`. It is the next concrete action.
- `[DIRTY]` means uncommitted changes. `[UNPUSHED]` means local commits not yet on GitHub. Either means a closeout missed that repo. Say so and name the repo.
- `uncommitted` as the date means STATUS.md itself is not committed yet.

## Pick one thread

Eric works many projects a day and loses the thread. After the list:

1. Name the flagged repos first, if any.
2. Offer the top 2–3 threads by date. Ask which one to pick up.
3. Do not start work on more than one. Park the rest.

Active threads are capped at 5 in the global MEMORY.md. If a new one is picked and the list is full, one must be parked first.

- The `--decisions` flag lists open questions, not NEXT lines. Use it for "what is waiting on me", and hand the list to `decision-audit` to actually decide.
- Repos under `_ARCHIVE`, `_to_delete`, `_OLD_` and `worktrees` are skipped on purpose.
- Windows reads `~/Desktop/DEV`. The same script runs there; the output will differ per machine.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/status-report

# Status Report

The recurring Applied Performance email to **Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf**, both addressed directly
("Kenny, Coach Ruf,"), about 270 words, with a one-page PDF and an internal record. Governed by **KR 4.1**
in `Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md`, read as a content checklist: shipped work, work in flight,
decisions needed, anything at risk, what's next.

**Primary job: alignment.** Chris and Kenny finish knowing what moved, what needs them, and what is at
risk. **Secondary job: credit** for work across sports beyond football and basketball; that is why the
report exists, so the sport tags and the coverage panel stay in every cycle.

**Design target: under 5 minutes of Eric's time.** The machine does the recall; the interview spends
his attention only on what no system can know.

## Paths

Keys come from `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (`macos` or `windows`, whichever
machine this is): `vault_root`, `vault_inbox_meetings`, `vault_output_ledger`, `vault_status_reports`,
`vault_status_log`, `portfolio_json`, `okr_doc`, `okr_tracker_dir`, `utilization_brief`,
`canonical_projects`, `fireflies_cli`. When `vault_root` does not exist, the config belongs to the other
machine: stop and fix it first.

Record template: `{vault_root}/Templates/status-report.md`, **Layer 2 and Layer 3 only**. Its Layer 1 (headed
sections, "Chris —" greeting, attached PDF) is the old layout; the email follows **Voice** below.

`weekly-review` is never a prerequisite. `html-to-pdf` is not needed: `scripts/onepager_pdf.py` renders.

## Step 1 — Establish the period

1. **Prior report** = the newest `*-status.md` in `{vault_status_reports}` (the folder also holds drafts,
   PDFs and HTML). Period start = its `period_end`; period end = today. With no prior record, start = 14
   days ago. Report number = prior `report_number` + 1.
2. **Missed fortnights widen the period.** The archive never has a gap.
3. **Sent or not.** A report counts as sent when its record says `sent: true` or its folder holds
   `YYYY-MM-DD-email-sent.txt`. When the prior report has neither, add "did report N go out?" to the
   Step 4 batch; an unconfirmed report stays unsent. If Eric says it never went out, set its record's
   `sent: never` (so no later run asks again); a `sent: never` report counts as answered. Period start =
   the `period_start` of the report after the newest sent one, so unsent content folds into this one.
4. **Send dates** fall every 14 days from 2026-08-24 (the first send, "Starting these updates every two
   weeks"): 2026-11-02, 11-16, 11-30, 12-14. The last is 12-14; the semester closes 12-18.
   `python3 -c "import datetime as d;b=d.date(2026,8,24);t=d.date.today();print(next(b+d.timedelta(14*n) for n in range(40) if b+d.timedelta(14*n)>t))"`
   prints the next date after today. The footer's "Next report" is the grid date after this report's own.
5. KR 4.1 is eight reports through 2026-12-18. Step 8 states how many are confirmed sent.

**Done when** you hold period start and end, the report number, the prior report's sent state, and the next
send date.

## Step 2 — Pull (no Eric involvement)

Read `SOURCES.md` (every source, its fallback, and what lies), then run these in parallel and ask Eric for
nothing obtainable here:

1. Meetings (Fireflies digest, with the vault copy as fallback).
2. Supervisor logs for the period: read first, they carry the operational two thirds.
3. Shipped artifacts from the ledger: the only source for Shipped.
4. Active job projects from the registry: In Progress only.
5. KR state from the OKR doc, the sport roster, the canonical project spine.

**Done when** each source has produced rows or a named degraded-source note for the record, and you have
the logged-days count.

## Step 3 — Draft before asking

Write a complete draft covering all five KR 4.1 items from the pull, as flat prose in the Voice below.
Cut to 5–6 projects with real motion; unmoved ones go to the record and the coverage panel. Tag every
Shipped and In Progress line with a sport: *(Volleyball)*, *(Football)*, *(Soccer)*, *(Dept-wide)*,
*(Cross-sport)*. Then list the gaps for Step 4.

**Done when** the draft exists and every gap is a question.

## Step 4 — Interview the gaps, in one batch

Ask once. Targeted questions come from the pull ("Three meetings Tuesday–Thursday have no notes. Anything
Chris needs from them?" / "Ledger shows nothing shipped this period; is that right?"), then the standing
ones. Read the merged supervisor log back as a list and ask "anything missing?" for the questions it
already answered (1–4); asking again is how the nightly ritual dies.

1. Equipment, installs, deliveries: what arrived, went in where, got phased out, who onboards.
2. Meetings held and staffing: who, what came out, cadence changes.
3. Conversations no transcript caught: hallway, text, sideline, phone.
4. Anything waiting on someone else: unanswered emails, pending approvals (they become the soft
   "passing that along" lines).
5. Anything about to go sideways that Chris and Kenny should hear from Eric first. Push here; an
   always-empty risk line means it is not used honestly.
6. Any ask: time at a meeting, a decision, a nudge.
7. Ideas worth parking, pitching or building.
8. What's next in the coming two weeks.

With thin coverage, add: "Any sport you touched that isn't showing up in my sources?"

Append each confirmed, unlogged ship to `{vault_output_ledger}` now: Step 5 checks Shipped lines against it.

**Done when** every gap has an answer or an explicit "nothing", and each confirmed Shipped line has a
ledger row.

## Step 5 — Assemble and check

Fill the Layer 2 and Layer 3 shapes from the template. Run every box; fix a failure, then rerun the whole
list from the top (a cut for word count can drop a sport tag or the only risk line).

- [ ] Email body is under 300 words (target 270). Count with `wc -w` on the body; state the count.
- [ ] Every Shipped line traces to a ledger row dated in the period.
- [ ] No endorsement claimed that does not exist: "our standard intake process", never "the approved process".
- [ ] Every Shipped and In Progress line carries a sport tag (the PDF carries the tags; the email's prose
      names the sport).
- [ ] Every ask names a person and a date. The email says them in Eric's soft register ("could use
      your read, Kenny, before the 13th"); the PDF states them plainly. An ask with no owner or date is
      cut or rewritten.
- [ ] No CMJ, ACWR or asymmetry-index jargon; B.A.I.R. spelled out once.
- [ ] Department names: Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, Applied Performance.
- [ ] The line is "standardized underneath, bespoke on top".
- [ ] Research reads as research, with no readiness or deployment claims.
- [ ] Risks are non-empty unless Eric confirmed nothing; ask once more before leaving them empty.
- [ ] An ask carried over from the prior report is flagged to Eric: two unanswered asks mean the email has
      failed at it and it needs raising in person.
- [ ] Email and PDF agree: every Shipped, In Progress, ask and risk in the email appears in the PDF with
      the same facts, sport tag and date. The PDF may carry more.
- [ ] The coverage panel is unpadded: untouched sports stay marked untouched.
- [ ] Meeting action items appear as work in flight, never as done.

**Done when** one full pass leaves every box ticked. Show Eric the draft only then.

## Step 6 — Emit

Three files in `{vault_status_reports}`:

1. **`YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — plain text, only what gets pasted: from "Kenny, Coach Ruf," to "Eric".
   No markdown, no header block, no cut list; a select-all copy goes into Outlook with zero cleanup.
2. **`YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf`** — copy `assets/one-pager.html` to `YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.html`, fill every
   `{{placeholder}}`, then run
   `python3 ~/.claude/skills/status-report/scripts/onepager_pdf.py render <html> <pdf>`
   (`python` on Windows). It measures first (budget 950px at 666px width) and refuses a file with
   placeholders left. Over budget, cut prose and keep the type at 9.6pt or larger. The page is a printed
   memorandum: single column, one serif family, letterspaced small-cap heads, one green hairline. Status
   dots, badges, bolded stat lines, progress bars and two-column grids stay out.
3. **`YYYY-MM-DD-status.md`** — the internal record in the template's Layer 3 shape, with frontmatter
   `report_number`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `next_send`, `sent: false`, `word_count`,
   `sources_degraded:`. Cuts and softened lines (what came out of the email, and why) go in a "Cut and
   softened" section; "Not for the report" stays candid.

Also print the email text in the reply.

**Upload the PDF to Drive** (Eric, 2026-10-31), through the API, never the Drive mount, into
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/03_REPORTS`:

```
cd "{vault_status_reports}" && gws drive +upload ./YYYY-MM-DD-onepager.pdf --parent 18lZZ4ep4pmK6upQfEcTUuLNlDdSAk5Au --name YYYY-MM-DD_Department_StatusReport_OnePager_Supervisors.pdf
```

Write the returned file id to the record as `drive_id:`. A re-render the same day uploads a new copy
beside the old one; never overwrite. Only the PDF goes up: the email and the record stay local.

**Send nothing and share nothing.** No Teams post, no Drive share link. The connected Gmail is Eric's
personal address; create no Gmail draft. Eric sends from Outlook on the work account, after he has read
the report.

**Done when** all three files exist, the measure printed a height at or under 950, the PDF is one page,
and the record holds the PDF's `drive_id`.

## Step 7 — Log

- Update `{canonical_projects}` with confirmed status, sport and KR.
- For each project reported as moved, run `/project update "<name>" "<note>"` (the `project` skill), and
  leave `portfolio.json` uncommitted.

**Done when** each moved project has an `updates[]` entry and the canonical list is current.

## Step 8 — Report to Eric

State: word count, report number, next send date, sports that appeared, anything the checks flagged, the
three file paths, the PDF's Drive id, and `N of D days logged` from the supervisor log, stated plainly ("6 of 14 days
logged, so the interview covered the other 8 from memory"). Add any stale-meeting or degraded-source note
from Step 2, and how many reports are confirmed sent toward KR 4.1's eight.

When this run hit a problem no Step 5 box covers, whether you caught it or Eric did while editing, end with
one proposed new checklist line and its reason. Add it to Step 5 on his yes.

**Done when** Eric has those items in one message.

---

## Voice

Read `{vault_status_reports}/2026-08-24-email-sent.txt` before drafting: the one report Eric sent, and the
reference for how he writes.

- Flat short paragraphs, one topic each, no section labels. KR 4.1 is the content checklist.
- One framing line up top, then straight in.
- "We" for department work, "I" for his own actions.
- Concrete and operational: equipment, buildings, people, dates; names people freely.
- Contractions throughout; plain-English edits that strip them make the email sound like someone else.
- Asks come last and land soft ("One ask I wanted to run past you both is whether…").
- Stalled things get passed along: "still haven't heard back. Passing that along in case a nudge is
  warranted."
- No attachment in the ordinary cycle; the PDF is for handing across a table.
- A quiet period is a legitimate report: "Nothing shipped this period" protects the word everywhere
  else. The email is five or six moving projects, never a 14-line roster.

# Status report: sources, fallbacks and traps

Step 2 of `SKILL.md` points here. Paths are config keys (`~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`).
Read this whole file before the pull.

## Meetings (`fireflies_cli`)

Preflight first: `{fireflies_cli} transcripts list --agent --data-source live 2>&1 | head -5`.
The key is in `~/.zshrc`; the local mirror is `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`.
`unable to open database file: out of memory (14)` means the mirror is missing, so run
`{fireflies_cli} sync` and retry.

Pull: `{fireflies_cli} digest --since <N>d --processed-only --agent` (N = days in the period; `--since`
takes `7d` or `24h`). It returns `meetings[]` with `title`, `date`, `gist`, `action_items`, `participants`.
Cross-check against `{vault_inbox_meetings}/YYYY-MM-DD_*.md`.

If the live pull fails, the report still builds (`meeting-sync` stops on an auth failure; this skill
carries on):

- Read `{vault_inbox_meetings}/*.md` for the period by the `YYYY-MM-DD_` prefix. The files have no YAML
  frontmatter; the header block (`## Key topics`, `## Decisions`, `## Action items`) is often empty, so
  read the Fireflies sections (`## Summary`, `### Overview`, `### Action Items`).
- Compare the newest meeting date to today. A gap over 2 days goes to Eric in Step 8: "Meeting data is
  stale through {DATE}; anything after that came only from the interview."
- Name the degraded source in the record's `sources_degraded:` frontmatter list.

`{fireflies_cli} action-items list --from <N> --agent` is **broken** (checked 2026-10-31): exit 0 and an
array of empty `{}` objects, which reads as "no open commitments". Take action items from the digest.
Flag any item open more than 14 days as a risk candidate.

Meeting action items are assignments, not outcomes. An action item never becomes a Shipped line.

## Supervisor logs (`vault_status_log`)

Every `YYYY-MM-DD.md` inside the period. `closeout` Step 0 writes them (the `interview-me` Part 0
wording is the format). They are the best source in the pull: equipment, installs, hallway
conversations and follow-ups awaiting a reply appear nowhere else.

- Merge `## Equipment & installs`, `## People & conversations`, `## Waiting on / risks` across the
  period; union every `sports:` array for the coverage panel.
- The wording is Eric's own; keep it.
- Count the files: `logged` of `days-in-period` goes to Step 8. A thin count is the number that says the
  nightly ritual lapsed. Never pad it. (2026-10-31: three logs exist, 09-07 to 09-14.)
- Zero logs never stops the run; Step 4 then covers everything.

## Shipped (`vault_output_ledger`)

The only source for Shipped. A markdown table, newest first:
`| Shipped | Artifact | What it is | Harvest |`, *Shipped* as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Match rows with
`^\| 2\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{2}` and filter by date. *What it is* runs to a paragraph: compress to one clause for
the email.

`portfolio.json` `stage: shipped` is not evidence: it marks projects shipped while stakeholder sign-off is
outstanding (Sport_Tech_Vetting was `shipped` while KR 1.2 showed Chris's sign-off pending). Stage feeds
In Progress only.

## In progress (`portfolio_json`)

The file is `{"meta", "projects", "ideas", "inbox"}`; rows live under `projects`. Keep `lane == "job"` and
`status == "active"` (7 rows on 2026-10-31; the other job rows are paused, merged, archived or done).
Use `next_action` and `updates[]` (`date`, `note`). `stage` is empty on most rows and `charter` exists on
a few, so lean on `updates[]`. Also read `{canonical_projects}` for each project's sport and KR.

The registry holds Eric's building work. A draft from the automated sources alone is about one third of
the report; the interview supplies the rest.

## KR state (`okr_doc`)

`Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27.md` is the only KR source. Its current cycle is Fall 2026 (7 KRs, written
2026-09-14). Report KR status from that file alone.

- `{okr_scoreboard}` and `okrs.yaml` score the retired Q1 summer set. Skip them.
- The cadence doc's KR table is a superseded set. Skip it.
- KR 4.1 is this report: 8 reports through 2026-12-18.

## Sport roster

The 17 varsity programs come from `{utilization_brief}` section "Recommendations by program" (15 rows; the
two XC / Track & Field rows each bundle two programs), and `{canonical_projects}` section "Sport
coverage" holds the evidence baseline. Read both; never list programs from memory. The brief says what each
program could use, so it is a roster and the coverage panel is the activity record.

## Optional

`{vault_root}/Inbox/weekly-review/*.md` inside the period, when present. The report never waits on it.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command for the end-of-day sequence: day log → loose ends → memory → STATUS and handoff → commit and push → one verdict.

Step 0 asks Eric one question at most. After his answer (or when Step 0 is skipped), run every
other step without pausing: invoking closeout authorizes the whole sequence. Commit and push is
standing-authorized for every DEV repo (each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine ends with it, and
unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other). On Windows or in Cowork,
read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Scope.** Every DEV repo with uncommitted or unpushed work (touched this session or not), plus
`~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory`.
A repo whose `CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local (DexaProject is the precedent) is committed,
not pushed, and listed.

**Clear to sign off when** the closing `where-was-i.py --sweep` (step 4) shows no `ACTION` line
except repos listed under "Still open" with their reason, no background job is still writing,
`.errors.log` is empty or its entries are reported, and every repo touched today has a STATUS entry
dated today with a concrete first `## Next` item, and every `card-check` gap is fixed. Questions
only Eric can answer (a receiver nobody named, a decision recorded under `## Open questions`) do
not block: `/startup` shows them tomorrow; list them under "Still open" and say "Clear to sign off".
Anything short of that: "Not clear", naming the one thing blocking.

If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and
note it. A risky fix goes under "Still open".

## Step 0 — Day log (once a day)

Closeout is the one end-of-day step Eric keeps, so it carries the two inputs the biweekly
`status-report` trusts: the supervisor log and the shipped ledger. Before 2026-10-31 they lived
only in `interview-me` and `harvest`, and both lapsed (last log 09-14, last ledger row 10-06).

`{vault_status_log}` is `vault_status_log` in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`.
When `{vault_status_log}/<today>.md` or `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` exists, today's log is
already taken (usually by `interview-me`): leave out the three Part 0 questions and keep only
question 4, and only when step 1 finds a candidate. No candidate and no Front Burner question
(step 2 below) as well: skip this step.

0. **Front Burner checks** (plan `project-triage/docs/plans/2026-10-31-front-burner-self-maintaining.md`):
   run `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py dates` and `... drift`. Resolve every line you
   can from evidence (STATUS dates, commits) with a cited `add-update` note. Every remaining line
   whose `needs_eric` is true (`--json`) becomes one more numbered question in step 2's batch:
   overdue step or no date → "done, new date, or no hard date?"; `off_board` → "start X?";
   `quiet` → "keep X or park it?". Ask every one, not just the first. Record answers the same day:
   one command per answer, `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py decide X <action>`:
   done → `done --step N`; new date for an overdue step → `redate --step N --date YYYY-MM-DD`;
   a date for a row that has none (`no_date`) → `redate --date YYYY-MM-DD` (no `--step`: it adds one); no hard date →
   `no-date [--step N] --reason "..." --source "..."`; an old "no hard date" still true →
   `confirm-no-date`; a row with a dated step and an old record → `drop-no-date` (no question
   needed); keep a quiet row → `keep-quiet`; "no,
   leave it off the board" → `keep-off` (stores the exact moment, so only later work is asked
   about). Start or park with `set-status`. Do not hand-edit these fields. Skipped lines are not
   blocking: list them under "Still open".

1. **Ship candidates.** Read today's dated `## Current state` lines in every repo touched today
   (the sweep in Step 1 lists them; `landed.py show --days 1` also works). A candidate is work
   handed to a person or put in use: sent, delivered, shared, presented, merged for a user, live.
   Drop any project that already has a row dated today in the ledger (`{vault_output_ledger}`).
2. **Ask once**, all at once, short answers accepted: the three Part 0 questions from
   `interview-me/SKILL.md` (that file holds their wording; left out when today's log is taken), plus:
   > 4. Did anything ship or go to someone today? I found: <candidates, or "nothing">.

   then 5, 6, ... : one per Front Burner `needs_eric` line from step 0.
3. **Write the log** (only when you asked the Part 0 questions) exactly as `interview-me` Part 0 says (output format, honest-zero rule,
   append to an existing file). On an honest zero, write the empty marker
   `{vault_status_log}/.asked-<today>` instead, so the next closeout today skips the ask.
4. **Each confirmed ship:** run the `harvest` skill for it. Eric's yes is the ship evidence harvest
   Step 1 needs; the ledger row is the required part, lesson articles only when harvest finds them.

**Done when** the log file or the marker exists for today and every confirmed ship has a ledger
row dated today.

## Step 1 — Sweep

- **Repo sweep:** `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s). It checks every git
  repo under `DEV/` (two levels) and the three config repos, and prints one line per repo needing
  attention; exit 1 means at least one `ACTION`. Another session, harness or machine may have left
  that work; name each such repo in the report. Flags:
  - `DIRTY`, `UNPUSHED`, `NO-UPSTREAM`, `BRANCH-AHEAD:<b>`, `BRANCH-UNPUSHED:<b>` (a local branch
    holding commits on no remote), `WORKTREE-DIRTY:<path>`: work not on GitHub. Step 4 pushes it.
  - `NOT-A-REPO`: a `.git` folder git cannot use, so the folder's work is tracked nowhere. List it;
    repair is project work, not closeout. It blocks only if this session wrote files there.
  - Info, never blocking: `STASH:<n>` (list it; leave the stash alone), `NO-REMOTE`, `DETACHED`
    (a pinned checkout), `LIVE` (session files the hooks rewrite every turn; the daily backup
    pushes them).
- **Background jobs** still running (shells, agents, workflows): wait for each to finish, or name
  it as the blocker. A job that writes after the push leaves work unpushed.
- **Registry drift:** `python3 <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is
  in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.macos.json`). It only reports. List every item under "Still
  open", any folder created this session first (a project started without a row). Fixing waits
  for a project session. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran: say so.
- Unfinished tasks from this session (TaskList), and anything promised to Eric this session and
  not delivered.

## Step 2 — Memory

Memory capture failing silently is Eric's top recurring worry; this step runs every time.

- **`~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`:** surface every entry, fix the hook issue if
  obvious, then archive and clear it as in claude-stack-doctor's `FIXES.md` → Memory pipeline
  (append to `.errors-ledger.log`, then `cp /dev/null`). The file is tracked in `global-memory`,
  so this happens before step 4's push.
- **Today's transcript** `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` exists and changed within
  the last few hours.
- **New durable decision or active thread:** update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md`
  (2,500-char cap; consolidate first) or write a Tier A memory with the `memory-write` skill.
- **Tier A stays on this machine** (its slug is built from the absolute path, which differs per
  machine). Every durable, project-scoped Tier A fact written today also goes into the repo:
  `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reason, the dated
  handoff for detail.

## Step 3 — STATUS, handoff, cards

**Handoff**, when real work happened (not just Q&A): `<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`;
workspace or system work with no single repo goes to `~/DEV/docs/handoffs/`
(`~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` is read-only history). Plain markdown that Codex,
Antigravity or a fresh Claude session can resume from:
- what was worked on and why
- decisions made, with the reasoning that would be lost
- exact paths of every file created or modified
- next actions, most important first
- anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)
- suggested skills: which ones the next session should invoke, by name

Link, don't copy: if a spec, plan, ADR, issue or commit already holds the detail, give its
path, URL or sha. Redact keys, passwords and personal data; the note is pushed to GitHub.

**`docs/STATUS.md`, in every repo touched, every time.** The next session reads it first, on
either machine, in any harness. Rewrite these sections in place, short:
- `## Current state`: two to five lines on where things stand today.
- `## Next`: most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to
  open); `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows it to Eric the next morning.
- `## Open questions`: each decision waiting on Eric as its own top-level bullet, the question and
  enough context to answer it without opening another file. `/startup` lists this section across
  repos, so write the question itself, never a pointer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …`
  or strike them (`~~…~~`). Leave the section empty when nothing waits.
- `## Gotchas`: anything that will bite the next session.

Over 20 KB, or more than 15 dated entries under `## Current state`: first move entries older than
14 days and finished `## Next` items, verbatim, to the end of
`docs/handoffs/STATUS-archive-<YYYY>-Q<n>.md`. The archive is a search root; entries move, they
are never deleted.

Then:
